s: Sociology - Module 1: Origin and Development of Sociology

q: 'Recognised and intended consequence of social action' best describes which concept?
e: Merton's term for consciously sought results.
s: Sociology - Module 1: Origin and Development of Sociology

q: The concept described as 'Ordinary, utilitarian and everyday aspects of life' is called:
e: The opposite pole to the sacred in Durkheim's scheme.
s: Sociology - Module 1: Origin and Development of Sociology

q: 'Das Kapital' is a famous work of:
e: The critique of political economy whose first volume appeared in 1867.
s: Sociology - Module 1: Origin and Development of Sociology

q: The classic text 'Risk Society' was produced by:
e: The 1986 analysis of manufactured risk in reflexive modernity.
s: Sociology - Module 1: Origin and Development of Sociology

q: Which term is defined as 'Overarching story claiming universal validity'?
e: Lyotard held that postmodernity has lost faith in such stories.
s: Sociology - Module 1: Origin and Development of Sociology

q: Choose the correct definition of Altruistic suicide.
o: Suicide caused by excessive social integration
Shared understanding between conscious social actors
Prison design enabling constant unseen surveillance
Condition in which representation replaces reality
e: The group's claims override the value of individual life.
s: Sociology - Module 1: Origin and Development of Sociology

q: Select the statement that applies to Position of sociology in Comte's hierarchy of sciences.
e: It is the last to reach the positive stage and depends on biology.
s: Sociology - Module 1: Origin and Development of Sociology

q: Alfred Schutz contributed to the discipline mainly through:
e: Schutz analysed the common-sense typifications of everyday life.
s: Sociology - Module 1: Origin and Development of Sociology

q: Select the author of the work 'The Structural Transformation of the Public Sphere'.
e: His 1962 historical account of bourgeois public debate.
s: Sociology - Module 1: Origin and Development of Sociology

q: 'The Gift' — identify the author.
e: The 1925 essay on reciprocity in archaic societies.
s: Sociology - Module 1: Origin and Development of Sociology

q: Two sources of Schutz's phenomenological sociology is best associated with:
e: He grounded subjective meaning in the structures of consciousness.
s: Sociology - Module 1: Origin and Development of Sociology

q: Goffman's guiding metaphor for social life is:
e: Actors, stages, scripts and audiences organise his analysis.
s: Sociology - Module 1: Origin and Development of Sociology

q: Which of the following best explains Mores?
o: Suicide caused by weak social integration
Strongly held norms carrying moral significance
Prison design enabling constant unseen surveillance
Legitimacy resting on exceptional personal qualities
e: Their violation attracts severe social sanction.
s: Sociology - Module 1: Origin and Development of Sociology

q: Anomic suicide refers to:
o: Action performed out of habit and custom
Suicide caused by breakdown of social regulation
Recurring pattern of interaction abstracted from content
Conversion of personal charisma into stable institutions
e: Occurs in periods of sudden economic or social disruption.
s: Sociology - Module 1: Origin and Development of Sociology

q: Traditional action — which of the following is correct?
o: Action driven by emotions and feeling states
Instrumentally rational action calculating means and ends
Action performed out of habit and custom
Legitimacy resting on custom and inherited status
e: It lies at the border of meaningful conduct.
s: Sociology - Module 1: Origin and Development of Sociology

q: William Graham Sumner is known for writing:
e: The 1906 work introducing folkways, mores and ethnocentrism.
s: Sociology - Module 1: Origin and Development of Sociology

q: Which of the following ideas is credited to Karl Mannheim?
e: Mannheim related systems of thought to the social position of thinkers.
s: Sociology - Module 1: Origin and Development of Sociology

q: Lewis Coser is remembered in this field for:
e: Coser showed that conflict can strengthen group boundaries and cohesion.
s: Sociology - Module 1: Origin and Development of Sociology

q: Choose the correct definition of Triad.
o: Suicide caused by excessive social integration
Suicide caused by weak social integration
e: It allows coalitions, mediation and the tertius gaudens.
s: Sociology - Module 1: Origin and Development of Sociology

q: Georg Simmel is best known for:
e: Simmel studied the recurring forms of sociation apart from their contents.
s: Sociology - Module 1: Origin and Development of Sociology

q: Thinker who said the history of all hitherto existing society is the history of class struggles is:
e: The opening proposition of The Communist Manifesto.
s: Sociology - Module 1: Origin and Development of Sociology

q: Edwin Sutherland authored which of the following?
e: The textbook presenting differential association theory.
s: Sociology - Module 1: Origin and Development of Sociology

q: In technical usage, 'Ideal type' denotes:
o: Suicide caused by weak social integration
e: A yardstick for comparison, not a moral or statistical ideal.
s: Sociology - Module 1: Origin and Development of Sociology

q: Who is associated with 'Concepts of folkways and mores'?
e: Sumner distinguished ordinary customs from morally charged norms.
s: Sociology - Module 1: Origin and Development of Sociology

q: Sociological imagination can be best understood as:
o: Shared beliefs and sentiments common to a society
Capacity to link personal troubles with public issues
Study of phenomena as they appear to consciousness
Process of interaction through which society is formed
e: Mills's term for grasping the interplay of biography and history.
s: Sociology - Module 1: Origin and Development of Sociology

q: Identify what is linked with Two sources of Schutz's phenomenological sociology.
e: He grounded subjective meaning in the structures of consciousness.
s: Sociology - Module 1: Origin and Development of Sociology

q: The book 'The Metropolis and Mental Life' is credited to:
e: The 1903 essay on the blase attitude of the city dweller.
s: Sociology - Module 1: Origin and Development of Sociology

q: Edmund Husserl authored which of the following?
o: The Phenomenology of the Social World
The Division of Labour in Society
Human Nature and the Social Order
Ideas: General Introduction to Pure Phenomenology
e: Husserl's 1913 programmatic work on phenomenological method.
s: Sociology - Module 1: Origin and Development of Sociology

q: Select the statement that applies to Weber's iron cage refers to.
o: Confinement of modern life by bureaucratic rationality
Conformity, innovation, ritualism, retreatism and rebellion
Written rules, hierarchy and technical qualification
e: Rational order hardens into an inescapable shell.
s: Sociology - Module 1: Origin and Development of Sociology

q: Whose work centres on 'Method of deconstruction'?
e: Derrida exposed the unstable oppositions on which Western texts rest.
s: Sociology - Module 1: Origin and Development of Sociology

q: Choose the correct definition of Symbolic interactionism.
o: Capacity to link personal troubles with public issues
Value created by labour beyond the wages paid
Study of society through shared meanings and symbols
Theory lying between working hypotheses and grand theory
e: Named by Blumer and grounded in the work of Mead.
s: Sociology - Module 1: Origin and Development of Sociology

q: Identify what is linked with Perspective that views society as an arena of inequality and struggle.
e: Associated with Marx, Dahrendorf, Coser and Mills.
s: Sociology - Module 1: Origin and Development of Sociology

q: Herbert Spencer is remembered in this field for:
e: Spencer compared social institutions to the organs of a living body.
s: Sociology - Module 1: Origin and Development of Sociology

q: Foucault's two methods of historical enquiry — identify the correct association.
e: Archaeology maps discursive rules; genealogy traces power relations.
s: Sociology - Module 1: Origin and Development of Sociology

q: Choose the correct definition of Social form.
o: Legitimacy resting on enacted rules and offices
Keeping personal values out of scientific analysis
Conversion of personal charisma into stable institutions
Recurring pattern of interaction abstracted from content
e: Conflict, exchange and domination are such forms for Simmel.
s: Sociology - Module 1: Origin and Development of Sociology

q: Which term is defined as 'Internalised attitude of the whole community'?
e: It emerges at the game stage of Mead's scheme.
s: Sociology - Module 1: Origin and Development of Sociology

q: What is meant by 'Role set'?
o: Arena of rational public debate independent of the state
Array of role relationships attached to a single status
Estrangement of the worker from labour and its product
Region where a performance is given before an audience
e: A teacher relates to pupils, parents, colleagues and inspectors.
s: Sociology - Module 1: Origin and Development of Sociology

q: Who is the author of 'The History of Sexuality'?
e: A multi-volume study of discourse, confession and biopower.
s: Sociology - Module 1: Origin and Development of Sociology

q: False consciousness — which of the following is correct?
o: Beliefs that conceal the real interests of a class
Estrangement of the worker from labour and its product
Region where performers relax out of the audience's view
Basic needs a social system must satisfy to survive
e: Engels's term for ideologically distorted awareness.
s: Sociology - Module 1: Origin and Development of Sociology

q: Sacred can be best understood as:
o: Value created by labour beyond the wages paid
Things set apart and forbidden, treated with reverence
Enclosed setting regulating all aspects of inmates' lives
Shared beliefs and sentiments common to a society
e: One pole of Durkheim's religious dichotomy.
s: Sociology - Module 1: Origin and Development of Sociology

q: Home institute of the Frankfurt School — identify the correct association.
e: Founded in 1923 and directed by Max Horkheimer from 1930.
s: Sociology - Module 1: Origin and Development of Sociology

q: The concept described as 'Suicide caused by breakdown of social regulation' is called:
e: Occurs in periods of sudden economic or social disruption.
s: Sociology - Module 1: Origin and Development of Sociology

q: Which of the following is correct about Two divisions of Comte's sociology?
o: Ownership of the means of production
e: The first studies order, the second studies progress.
s: Sociology - Module 1: Origin and Development of Sociology

q: 'The Social System' is a famous work of:
e: His 1951 statement of structural functional theory.
s: Sociology - Module 1: Origin and Development of Sociology

q: Reification — which of the following is correct?
o: Person whose attitudes matter most in forming the self
Practices by which actions are made observable and reportable
Array of role relationships attached to a single status
Treating human social relations as though they were things
e: Lukacs derived it from Marx's commodity fetishism.
s: Sociology - Module 1: Origin and Development of Sociology

q: The writer of 'The Elementary Forms of the Religious Life' is:
e: His 1912 study of Australian totemism and the sacred.
s: Sociology - Module 1: Origin and Development of Sociology

q: False consciousness refers to:
o: Practices by which actions are made observable and reportable
Array of role relationships attached to a single status
Estrangement of the worker from labour and its product
Beliefs that conceal the real interests of a class
e: Engels's term for ideologically distorted awareness.
s: Sociology - Module 1: Origin and Development of Sociology

q: 'Method of deconstruction' — this is the contribution of:
e: Derrida exposed the unstable oppositions on which Western texts rest.
s: Sociology - Module 1: Origin and Development of Sociology

q: Ethnomethodology — which of the following is correct?
o: Person whose attitudes matter most in forming the self
Region where performers relax out of the audience's view
Study of methods people use to make sense of everyday life
Region where a performance is given before an audience
e: Garfinkel treated social order as an ongoing accomplishment.
s: Sociology - Module 1: Origin and Development of Sociology

q: Which work was written by Jean Baudrillard?
e: The 1981 work on signs, simulation and hyperreality.
s: Sociology - Module 1: Origin and Development of Sociology

q: 'Rejection of universal truth claims' refers to:
o: Postmodernism's attitude to universal truth claims
Merton's five modes of individual adaptation
Founder of the sociology of knowledge
e: Knowledge is treated as local, plural and contingent.
s: Sociology - Module 1: Origin and Development of Sociology

q: 'Structure and Function in Primitive Society' — identify the author.
e: Essays defining structural functionalism in social anthropology.
s: Sociology - Module 1: Origin and Development of Sociology

q: 'Concept of conspicuous consumption' — this is the contribution of:
e: The leisure class displays wealth through visible waste.
s: Sociology - Module 1: Origin and Development of Sociology

q: Choose the correct definition of Gemeinschaft.
o: Attribute that deeply discredits the person who bears it
Community based on natural will and close personal ties
Class conscious of its interests and organised for action
Practices by which actions are made observable and reportable
e: Tonnies's type exemplified by village and kin group.
s: Sociology - Module 1: Origin and Development of Sociology

q: Choose the correct definition of Zweckrational action.
o: Legitimacy resting on enacted rules and offices
Ordinary, utilitarian and everyday aspects of life
Instrumentally rational action calculating means and ends
Keeping personal values out of scientific analysis
e: One of Weber's four types of social action.
s: Sociology - Module 1: Origin and Development of Sociology

q: The classic text 'Das Kapital' was produced by:
e: The critique of political economy whose first volume appeared in 1867.
s: Sociology - Module 1: Origin and Development of Sociology

q: The name Georg Lukacs is connected with:
e: Commodity relations make social relations appear as relations between things.
s: Sociology - Module 1: Origin and Development of Sociology

q: Choose the correct statement about W.I. Thomas.
e: Situations defined as real are real in their consequences.
s: Sociology - Module 1: Origin and Development of Sociology

q: Who is generally regarded as the father of Indian sociology?
e: Ghurye built the Bombay department and trained the first generation of Indian sociologists.

q: India's first department of sociology was established in 1919 at:
e: The Bombay department began in 1919, with Patrick Geddes as its first head.

q: The Lucknow School of Indian sociology is associated with:
e: Radhakamal Mukerjee, D.P. Mukerji and D.N. Majumdar formed the Lucknow group.

q: The journal 'Contributions to Indian Sociology' was founded by:
e: Dumont and Pocock launched it in 1957 to promote an Indological sociology.

q: The Indian Sociological Society was founded in:
e: G.S. Ghurye founded it in 1951; it publishes the Sociological Bulletin.

q: The Indological approach in Indian sociology relies chiefly on:
e: It interprets Indian society through the Vedas, Dharmashastras and epics.

q: Which of the following is NOT an exponent of the Indological approach?
e: Desai used a Marxist, historical-materialist framework.

q: The Marxist perspective in Indian sociology is best represented by:
e: Desai analysed Indian nationalism as a product of colonial capitalism.

q: 'Social Background of Indian Nationalism' was written by:
e: Desai traced nationalism to the material changes wrought by British rule.

q: D.P. Mukerji held that the study of Indian society must begin with:
o: Tradition, understood as a living force
e: He insisted that the Indian sociologist must be a sociologist of tradition.

q: According to D.P. Mukerji, the three principles of change internal to Indian tradition are:
e: To these he added the external principle of conflict or class struggle.

q: 'Modernisation of Indian Tradition' was written by:
e: Singh combined structural and cultural analysis of Indian social change.

q: The concept of sanskritisation was introduced by M.N. Srinivas in his study of:
e: Religion and Society among the Coorgs of South India appeared in 1952.

q: Sanskritisation refers to the process by which a lower caste:
o: Adopts the customs and rituals of a higher caste
e: It is a claim to higher rank through emulation of twice-born practice.

q: Which of the following is NOT true of sanskritisation?
o: It is a process of cultural mobility
It brings positional change in the caste system
It changes the structure of the caste system itself
It may involve giving up meat and liquor
e: Srinivas stressed that it produces positional, not structural, change.

q: A caste that has prospered adopts vegetarianism, teetotalism and the sacred thread. This is:
e: These are classic ritual markers of a sanskritising caste.

q: Besides the Brahmanical model, Srinivas later recognised other models of sanskritisation, namely:
e: He allowed for Kshatriya, Vaishya and Jat reference models as well.

q: Westernisation, as used by Srinivas, refers to changes brought about by:
o: Over a century and a half of British rule
e: It covers changes in technology, institutions, ideology and values.

q: Which of the following is NOT one of the attributes of a dominant caste as listed by Srinivas?
e: Economic and numerical strength and political power matter more than ritual rank.

q: Srinivas's ethnographic classic 'The Remembered Village' describes:
e: Srinivas rewrote it from memory after his notes were destroyed by fire.

q: Andre Beteille's 'Caste, Class and Power' is a study of the village of:
e: Sripuram in Tanjore district showed the growing divergence of the three dimensions.

q: S.C. Dube's 'Indian Village' is based on fieldwork in:
e: Shamirpet lies near Hyderabad in present-day Telangana.

q: The concepts of 'great tradition' and 'little tradition' were introduced by:
e: Redfield distinguished the reflective tradition of the few from the folk tradition.

q: Upward spread of a local folk practice into the wider Sanskritic tradition is called:
e: McKim Marriott coined the pair universalisation and parochialisation.

q: 'Homo Hierarchicus' was written by:
e: Dumont's 1966 work treats caste as a system of ideas and values.

q: For Louis Dumont, the fundamental principle underlying the caste system is:
o: The opposition of pure and impure
e: Hierarchy is the encompassing of the opposite by the principle of purity.

q: According to Dumont, in the caste system status is:
o: Separated from and superior to power
e: The disjunction of status and power distinguishes India in his account.

q: Dumont contrasted 'Homo Hierarchicus' of India with the Western:
e: Western society is founded on the ideology of the equal individual.

q: Dumont's approach to caste is often criticised as:
o: A book view rather than a field view
e: Critics argue that he privileged textual ideology over lived practice.

q: Which sociologist argued that caste should be seen in terms of difference rather than hierarchy?
e: Gupta emphasised competing caste ideologies rather than a single hierarchy.

q: B.R. Ambedkar described caste essentially as:
e: He called it an ascending scale of reverence and a descending scale of contempt.

q: Ambedkar's celebrated undelivered 1936 address was titled:
e: It was prepared for the Jat-Pat Todak Mandal, which then cancelled the meeting.

q: Ambedkar led the Mahad Satyagraha of 1927 to secure:
o: The right to draw water from a public tank
e: The struggle at Chavdar tank asserted Dalit rights to public water.

q: Ambedkar argued that caste could not be destroyed without destroying:
e: He held that the religious sanction behind caste had to be broken.

q: Kancha Ilaiah's 'Why I Am Not a Hindu' argues from the standpoint of:
e: He contrasts productive Dalit-Bahujan culture with Brahminical values.

q: Gail Omvedt's writings are chiefly concerned with:
e: She studied the non-Brahmin movement, Phule, Ambedkar and new social movements.

q: The Subaltern Studies group was founded by:
e: Guha edited the first volume, published in 1982.

q: In subaltern historiography, 'subaltern' denotes:
o: Groups subordinated by class, caste, gender or office
e: The usage derives from Gramsci's notion of subordinate groups.

q: Jyotirao Phule's work 'Gulamgiri' (1873) attacked:
e: Phule founded the Satyashodhak Samaj to oppose priestly supremacy.

q: The Self-Respect Movement in Tamil Nadu was led by:
e: Periyar campaigned against caste, ritual and Brahmin dominance from 1925.

q: The slogan 'One caste, one religion, one God for man' was given by:
e: Narayana Guru's teaching guided the social reform movement in Kerala.

q: Ayyankali is remembered chiefly for the struggle for:
o: Rights of Dalits in Travancore including schooling
e: He founded the Sadhu Jana Paripalana Sangham in 1907.

q: The Vaikom Satyagraha of 1924-25 demanded:
o: The right of avarna castes to use the roads around the temple
e: It was a landmark struggle against caste-based spatial exclusion in Travancore.

q: The Temple Entry Proclamation of Travancore was issued in:
e: Chithira Thirunal Balarama Varma opened state temples to all Hindus in 1936.

q: 'Kinship Organisation in India' was written by:
e: Karve mapped regional kinship patterns across four cultural zones.

q: Iravati Karve divided India into how many kinship zones?
e: Northern, central, southern and eastern zones.

q: A distinctive feature of the southern kinship zone described by Karve is:
o: Preference for cross-cousin and uncle-niece marriage
e: Marriage typically consolidates existing kin ties in the south.

q: In the northern kinship zone, marriage is regulated mainly by:
e: The four-gotra rule and village exogamy prohibit marriage with known kin.

q: Descent traced exclusively through the mother's line is called:
e: The Nayars of Kerala and the Khasis of Meghalaya are classic examples.

q: Which of the following communities is NOT matrilineal?
e: Jats follow patrilineal descent and patrilocal residence.

q: The matrilineal joint family household of Kerala is known as:
e: The tharavad held property in common under a karanavan.

q: The eldest male manager of a Nair tharavad is the:
e: He managed the property of the matrilineal joint family.

q: The system of inheritance through the female line in Kerala is called:
e: Makkathayam is the corresponding patrilineal system.

q: The pre-puberty tali-tying ritual among the Nayars was called:
e: Kathleen Gough analysed it in her study of Nayar marriage.

q: Kathleen Gough's classic fieldwork concerned:
e: Her work on Nayar marriage prompted a rethinking of the definition of marriage.

q: The Kerala Joint Hindu Family System (Abolition) Act was passed in:
e: It ended the joint family system and converted holdings into individual shares.

q: Fraternal polyandry, in which several brothers share one wife, is reported among the:
e: It is also reported among the Khasa of Jaunsar-Bawar and in Ladakh.

q: Marriage of a widow with the younger brother of her deceased husband is:
e: The junior form is anticipatory when the brother is younger.

q: A widower marrying his deceased wife's sister is practising:
e: Sororate preserves the alliance between the two families.

q: Marriage with the mother's brother's daughter is an example of:
e: It is widely preferred in South India and is prohibited in the North.

q: A Brahmin man marries a woman of a lower caste. Such a union is termed:
e: Anuloma or hypergamy is marriage 'with the grain' of the caste order.

q: A woman of a higher caste marrying a man of a lower caste is called:
e: Pratiloma or hypogamy was traditionally strongly disapproved.

q: Caste in India is essentially:
e: Marriage within the jati is the defining rule of the caste system.

q: Marriage within the same gotra is forbidden among most north Indian Hindus. This is an example of:
e: Gotra exogamy prohibits marriage within the patrilineal clan.

q: A married couple sets up its own separate household away from both sets of parents. This residence is:
e: Neolocal residence is increasingly common among urban salaried couples.

q: Residence of a married couple with the husband's mother's brother is:
e: Avunculocal residence occurs in some matrilineal societies.

q: The traditional hereditary exchange of goods and services between castes in an Indian village is:
e: The landowning jajman is served by hereditary kamins or purjans.

q: In the jajmani system, the patron who receives services is called the:
e: The service castes are the kamins or prajas.

q: A household consists of a man, his wife, their married sons with wives and children, sharing one kitchen. This is a:
e: Common residence, kitchen, property and worship define the classical joint family.

q: The manager and head of a Hindu joint family is known as the:
e: The karta administers the coparcenary property on behalf of members.

q: I.P. Desai's study of Mahuva concluded that:
o: The joint family had completely disappeared
Nuclear families are unknown in Gujarat
Jointness in relationships persists even where residence is nuclear
Urbanisation has no effect on the family
e: He distinguished residential jointness from functional jointness.

q: A.M. Shah argued that variation in Indian household composition is best explained by:
o: The developmental cycle of the domestic group
e: Households move between simple and complex forms over time.

q: 'Family and Kinship: A Study of the Pandits of Rural Kashmir' was written by:
e: Madan examined the household, marriage and the idea of non-renunciation.

q: The joint-nuclear debate in Indian family studies is mainly about:
o: Whether marriage is a sacrament or a contract
Whether the joint family is breaking down into nuclear units
Whether descent is patrilineal or matrilineal
e: Scholars dispute the pace and meaning of the supposed decline.

q: Which of the following is NOT usually cited as a cause of the weakening of the joint family?
o: Increase in the size of agricultural holdings
e: Fragmentation, not enlargement, of holdings has pressed on joint living.

q: According to Hindu tradition, marriage is regarded primarily as:
e: It is one of the sixteen samskaras and is ideally indissoluble.

q: In Muslim personal law, marriage (nikah) is regarded as:
e: Nikah is a contract requiring offer, acceptance and mahr.

q: Mahr in Muslim marriage refers to:
o: Dowry given by the bride's family
Payment or settlement due from the husband to the wife
A gift to the officiating priest
e: Mahr is the wife's right and is settled at the time of the contract.

q: Relatives connected through blood are called:
e: Relatives acquired through marriage are affinal kin.

q: A person's brother's wife is an example of:
e: She is a primary kin of one's primary kin, hence secondary.

q: A father-in-law never addresses his son's wife directly and withdraws when she enters. This kinship usage is:
e: Avoidance regulates contact between relatives of the opposite sex in some kin positions.

q: Free teasing and banter permitted between a man and his wife's younger sister illustrates:
e: Radcliffe-Brown analysed joking relationships as institutionalised disrespect.

q: Referring to a woman as 'the mother of Ravi' rather than by her own name is:
e: Teknonymy names a person through his or her child.

q: The custom in which the husband observes restrictions and mimics the wife at childbirth is:
e: It has been reported among some tribal groups in India.

q: Special respect and ritual importance given to the father's sister is called:
e: The corresponding special role of the mother's brother is the avunculate.

q: A kinship terminology that merges father and father's brother under one term is:
e: Classificatory terms group several distinct relatives together.

q: A descent group whose members can actually trace their links to a known common ancestor is a:
e: A clan claims common descent that cannot be genealogically traced.

q: Descent reckoned through the father for some purposes and through the mother for others is:
e: Double unilineal descent combines patrilineal and matrilineal groupings.

q: G.S. Ghurye listed several features of caste. Which of the following is NOT among them?
o: Restrictions on feeding and social intercourse
e: Ghurye listed the lack of unrestricted choice of occupation as a feature.

q: How many features of the caste system did G.S. Ghurye enumerate in 'Caste and Race in India'?
e: His classic list contains six features, beginning with segmental division.

q: Herbert Risley explained caste origins chiefly in terms of:
o: Racial difference and the nasal index
e: Risley's racial theory in The People of India is now rejected.

q: The theory that the caste system grew out of the absorption of tribes into Hindu society is associated with:
e: Bose described the Hindu method of tribal absorption.

q: Verrier Elwin initially advocated for Indian tribes a policy of:
e: His later position moved towards integration with safeguards.

q: The 'tribe-caste continuum' suggests that:
o: Tribes and castes are entirely separate
Tribal groups may gradually be absorbed into the caste order
Tribes are a colonial invention only
e: Surajit Sinha and others documented tribes becoming jatis.

q: Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes are specified under which Articles of the Constitution?
e: Article 341 deals with Scheduled Castes and Article 342 with Scheduled Tribes.

q: The Mandal Commission, which recommended reservation for Other Backward Classes, submitted its report in:
e: The B.P. Mandal report of 1980 was implemented from 1990.

q: The Mandal Commission recommended reservation for OBCs to the extent of:
e: This was upheld with conditions in the Indra Sawhney judgment of 1992.

q: The first Backward Classes Commission of 1953 was chaired by:
e: The Kalelkar Commission reported in 1955.

q: Untouchability is abolished by which Article of the Constitution of India?
e: Article 17 abolishes untouchability and forbids its practice in any form.

q: Rajni Kothari argued that in independent India:
o: Caste is purely a ritual matter
Politics has become casteist and caste has become politicised
e: His essay on caste in Indian politics stressed mutual transformation.

q: The concept of 'Brahmanical patriarchy' was developed by:
e: It links the control of women's sexuality to the maintenance of caste purity.

q: Leela Dube's writings are chiefly concerned with:
e: She studied how kinship structures shape the position of women.

q: The Hindu Marriage Act was enacted in:
e: It codified monogamy, conditions of marriage and grounds for divorce.

q: Which Act allows marriage between persons of any religion without conversion?
e: The Special Marriage Act provides a secular civil form of marriage.

q: The Hindu Succession (Amendment) Act of 2005 gave daughters:
e: Daughters became coparceners in joint family property on the same terms as sons.

q: The minimum legal age of marriage for women under the Prohibition of Child Marriage Act, 2006 is:
e: For men the prescribed minimum age is 21 years.

q: The Child Marriage Restraint Act of 1929 is popularly known as the:
e: It is named after Har Bilas Sarda, who piloted the Bill.

q: A family unit consisting of a woman and her children, with the husband largely absent, is described as:

e: It replaced the earlier GDI and GEM in the Human Development Report.

q: The Sustainable Development Goals were adopted by the United Nations in:
e: The 2030 Agenda was adopted in September 2015 and took effect in 2016.

q: How many Sustainable Development Goals are there?
e: The 17 goals contain 169 targets.

q: The Millennium Development Goals, which preceded the SDGs, numbered:
e: The eight MDGs covered the period 2000 to 2015.

q: Sustainable Development Goal 5 relates to:
e: SDG 5 seeks gender equality and the empowerment of all women and girls.

q: The definition of sustainable development as development that meets present needs without compromising future generations comes from:
e: Our Common Future was published by the Brundtland Commission in 1987.

q: The United Nations Conference on the Human Environment was held in 1972 at:
e: It led to the creation of the United Nations Environment Programme.

q: The headquarters of the United Nations Environment Programme is at:
e: UNEP was established in 1972 with its seat in Kenya.

q: World Environment Day is observed on:
e: It commemorates the opening of the Stockholm Conference in 1972.

q: The Earth Summit of 1992 was held at:
e: It produced Agenda 21, the UNFCCC and the Convention on Biological Diversity.

q: The Kyoto Protocol, which set binding emission targets for developed countries, was adopted in:
e: It was adopted in 1997 and entered into force in 2005.

q: Under the Paris Agreement of 2015, states agreed to hold the rise in global average temperature to:
o: Well below 2 degrees Celsius above pre-industrial levels
e: Parties also agreed to pursue efforts to limit the rise to 1.5 degrees.

q: The Montreal Protocol of 1987 deals with:
o: Substances that deplete the ozone layer
e: It phased out chlorofluorocarbons and related compounds.

q: The Ramsar Convention of 1971 concerns the conservation of:
e: India has designated a number of Ramsar sites, including three in Kerala.

q: The Basel Convention of 1989 regulates:
e: It restricts the export of hazardous waste to developing countries.

q: The Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change was established in 1988 by:
e: The IPCC assesses the science relating to climate change.

q: The principal greenhouse gas emitted by human activity is:
e: Burning of fossil fuels is the largest single source.

q: Which of the following is NOT a greenhouse gas?
e: Molecular nitrogen does not absorb infrared radiation.

q: Paddy cultivation and livestock rearing are major sources of which greenhouse gas?
e: Anaerobic decomposition in flooded fields releases methane.

q: The ozone layer that shields the earth from ultraviolet radiation lies in the:
e: The ozone hole was first detected over Antarctica.

q: The National Forest Policy of 1988 set a target of bringing under forest or tree cover:
o: 33 per cent of the geographical area
15 per cent of the geographical area
23 per cent of the geographical area
50 per cent of the geographical area
e: For hill and mountain regions the target is two-thirds.

q: The India State of Forest Report is published by:
e: The Forest Survey of India at Dehradun publishes it every two years.

q: The Chipko Movement began in 1973 in:
e: Villagers of Reni, led by Gaura Devi, hugged trees to prevent felling.

q: Which of the following leaders is NOT associated with the Chipko Movement?
e: Medha Patkar leads the Narmada Bachao Andolan.

q: The Appiko Movement of 1983, modelled on Chipko, took place in:
e: It began in the Uttara Kannada district of Karnataka.

q: The Narmada Bachao Andolan is chiefly a movement against:
e: The Sardar Sarovar Project is its main focus.

q: The Silent Valley Movement in Kerala was directed against:
o: A hydroelectric project across the Kunthipuzha
e: The project was abandoned and Silent Valley became a National Park in 1984.

q: Rachel Carson's 'Silent Spring' (1962) drew attention to the dangers of:
e: It is widely credited with launching the modern environmental movement.

q: The concept of the 'tragedy of the commons' was put forward by:
e: Hardin argued that unregulated common resources tend to be over-used.

q: 'The Limits to Growth' (1972) was a report prepared for the:
e: It modelled the consequences of exponential growth on a finite planet.

q: The Bhopal gas tragedy of December 1984 was caused by the leak of:
e: The gas escaped from the Union Carbide pesticide plant.

q: Minamata disease, caused by industrial effluent, results from poisoning by:
e: Itai-itai disease, by contrast, is caused by cadmium.

q: The Central Pollution Control Board was constituted under the Act of:
e: The Water (Prevention and Control of Pollution) Act, 1974 created it.

q: The Environment (Protection) Act was enacted in the aftermath of the Bhopal disaster in:
e: It is an umbrella legislation giving wide powers to the Central Government.

q: The National Green Tribunal was established under an Act of:
e: It provides for effective disposal of cases relating to environmental protection.

q: Environmental Impact Assessment became mandatory for specified projects in India through a notification of:
e: The 1994 notification was replaced by a revised notification in 2006.

q: Michael Cernea's model of the risks of displacement is known as the:
e: It lists landlessness, joblessness, homelessness and other risks.

q: Which of the following is NOT one of the impoverishment risks identified by Cernea?
e: The risks are all forms of loss, not gain.

q: The Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act was passed in:
e: It replaced the colonial Land Acquisition Act of 1894.

q: Under the 2013 land acquisition law, compensation in rural areas may be up to:
e: In urban areas the multiplier is two times the market value.

q: A large irrigation dam submerges twelve villages and the residents are moved to a resettlement colony far from their fields. The most accurate description is:
e: Displacement caused by a development project is involuntary resettlement.

q: Tribal communities are disproportionately affected by development-induced displacement in India mainly because:
o: Mineral and forest resources are concentrated in their habitats
e: Mining, dams and industry are located in resource-rich tribal regions.

q: The Forest Rights Act, which recognises the rights of forest dwelling communities, was enacted in:
e: It recognises individual and community forest rights.

q: Joint Forest Management in India was formally introduced through a circular issued in:
e: It involves village forest committees in protection and benefit sharing.

q: Which of the following is a renewable but exhaustible resource?
e: Groundwater replenishes naturally but can be depleted by over-extraction.

q: Excessive extraction of groundwater in an agricultural belt leads most directly to:
o: Falling water tables and drying of wells
e: Over-extraction beyond recharge lowers the water table.

q: Under the Solid Waste Management Rules, 2016, households are required to segregate waste into:
o: Biodegradable, non-biodegradable and domestic hazardous waste
e: Source segregation is the first duty of the waste generator.

q: The principle of '3R' in waste management stands for:
e: Reduction at source is preferred over recycling.

q: Extended Producer Responsibility means that:
o: Producers are responsible for the end-of-life management of their products
Waste is exported to other countries
e: It is applied to plastic, electronic and battery waste in India.

q: Composting of kitchen waste is an example of the treatment of:
e: Aerobic composting and biogas plants handle organic wet waste.

q: The Swachh Bharat Mission was launched on:
e: It was launched on Gandhi Jayanti with sanitation as its central goal.

q: The Haritha Karma Sena in Kerala is engaged mainly in:
o: Door-to-door collection and management of waste
e: These women's groups work with local bodies under the Kudumbashree network.

q: A panchayat sets up a plant to convert market waste into biogas and manure. This best illustrates:
e: Treating waste close to its source is the core of decentralised management.

q: Ester Boserup's 'Woman's Role in Economic Development' (1970) is the founding text of which approach?
e: The WID approach sought to integrate women into existing development programmes.

q: The Gender and Development (GAD) approach differs from the WID approach chiefly in that it:
o: Examines unequal power relations between women and men
e: GAD analyses socially constructed relations rather than women in isolation.

q: Caroline Moser's 'triple role' of women refers to:
o: Reproductive, productive and community managing work
e: Gender planning must recognise all three kinds of work.

q: Practical gender needs, as distinct from strategic gender needs, relate to:
o: Immediate necessities such as water, fuel and health care
Changing the sexual division of labour
e: Strategic needs challenge the structures of subordination themselves.

q: Gender auditing is best described as:
o: Counting the number of women employees only
Systematic examination of whether policies, budgets and practices promote gender equality
Auditing the accounts of women's organisations
e: It assesses institutional culture, programmes and resource allocation.

q: Gender budgeting in the Union Budget of India was formally introduced with a gender budget statement from:
e: The statement reports allocations for women in ministries and departments.

q: Amartya Sen's approach to development emphasises:
o: Expansion of human capabilities and freedoms
e: Development as Freedom treats freedom as both the means and the end.

q: Amartya Sen's phrase 'missing women' refers to:
o: The deficit of women in populations due to discrimination and neglect
Women absent from the labour force
e: It is reflected in adverse sex ratios in parts of Asia.

q: Vandana Shiva is best known in development debates for her:
e: She links the exploitation of nature with the subordination of women.

q: Bina Agarwal's 'A Field of One's Own' argues that the key to women's empowerment in South Asia is:
e: Land rights affect welfare, efficiency, equality and empowerment.

q: Naila Kabeer analyses empowerment in terms of:
e: Empowerment involves the ability to make strategic life choices.

q: Muhammad Yunus, awarded the Nobel Peace Prize in 2006, is associated with:
e: Group lending to poor women became a model for microfinance.

q: A self-help group of twenty women pools small monthly savings and lends internally before taking a bank loan. This sequence illustrates:
o: Thrift and credit leading to bank linkage
e: Internal lending builds the credit discipline required for SHG bank linkage.

q: The Mahatma Gandhi National Rural Employment Guarantee Act was passed by Parliament in:
e: The Act was notified in September 2005 and came into force in February 2006.

q: MGNREGS guarantees how many days of wage employment in a financial year to a rural household?
e: Additional days may be provided in notified drought-affected areas.

q: Under MGNREGS, at least what proportion of beneficiaries must be women?
e: The Act prescribes a minimum of one-third women beneficiaries.

q: Under MGNREGS, an unemployment allowance becomes payable if work is not provided within:
e: The applicant is entitled to work within fifteen days of applying.

q: Under MGNREGS, work should ordinarily be provided within a radius of:
e: If work is beyond 5 km, an extra wage allowance is payable.

q: Which body recommends the works to be taken up under MGNREGS and conducts social audit?
e: The gram sabha is the primary forum for planning and social audit.

q: MGNREGS is legally a rights-based programme because:
o: Employment is a legal entitlement enforceable by the worker
It is funded by the World Bank
It targets only below poverty line families
e: It is self-selecting and not restricted to BPL households.

q: The Integrated Rural Development Programme was launched in:
e: It aimed at self-employment for rural families below the poverty line.

q: Which programme was launched in 1999 by merging IRDP, TRYSEM and DWCRA?
e: SGSY was a holistic self-employment programme based on SHGs.

q: The National Rural Livelihoods Mission, also called Aajeevika, was launched in:
e: It was restructured from SGSY and later named DAY-NRLM.

q: The Antyodaya Anna Yojana is meant for:
o: The poorest of the poor among ration card holders
e: It provides highly subsidised foodgrain to the most destitute families.

q: The National Social Assistance Programme, launched in 1995, provides:
o: Old age, widow and disability pensions and family benefit
e: It gives effect to the directive principles on public assistance.

q: Pradhan Mantri Gram Sadak Yojana, launched in 2000, aims at:
o: All-weather road connectivity to unconnected habitations
e: Connectivity is intended to improve access to markets and services.

q: The 73rd Constitutional Amendment Act relating to panchayats was passed in:
e: It came into force on 24 April 1993, now observed as Panchayati Raj Day.

q: The 73rd Amendment inserted which Part and Schedule into the Constitution?
e: The Eleventh Schedule lists 29 subjects for devolution to panchayats.

q: The Eleventh Schedule of the Constitution contains how many subjects?
e: The Twelfth Schedule, for municipalities, contains 18 subjects.

q: Article 243D of the Constitution provides for reservation of seats in panchayats for women to the extent of not less than:
e: Many states, including Kerala, have raised this to fifty per cent.

q: Kerala raised the reservation for women in local self-government institutions to fifty per cent in:
e: The enhanced reservation applied from the 2010 local body elections.

q: The committee of 1957 that recommended a three-tier system of Panchayati Raj was headed by:
e: The Balwant Rai Mehta Committee proposed democratic decentralisation.

q: Panchayati Raj was first inaugurated in India on 2 October 1959 in:
e: Jawaharlal Nehru inaugurated it at Nagaur in Rajasthan.

q: Kudumbashree, the poverty eradication mission of Kerala, was launched in:
e: It was inaugurated at Malappuram on 17 May 1998.

q: The three-tier structure of Kudumbashree consists of:
o: Gram sabha, gram panchayat and zilla parishad
Neighbourhood Group, Area Development Society and Community Development Society
e: NHGs federate into ADS at ward level and into CDS at local body level.

q: The grassroots unit of Kudumbashree at the level of ten to twenty families is the:
e: The Neighbourhood Group is also called ayalkoottam.

q: The Community Development Society of Kudumbashree functions at the level of:
e: The ADS operates at ward level and the CDS at local body level.

q: Membership of a Kudumbashree Neighbourhood Group is open to:
o: Only women below the poverty line
One adult woman from each family
e: Preference is given to women from families identified as at risk.

q: Kudumbashree identifies poor families using:
o: A nine-point index of non-monetary deprivation indicators
e: Families meeting four or more of the risk indicators are treated as poor.

q: Balasabhas organised under Kudumbashree are collectives of:
e: They aim at the development and participation of children of member families.

q: The Ashraya project of Kudumbashree is intended for:
e: It identifies the most destitute and provides a package of support.

q: A Kudumbashree group takes a bank loan and starts a unit making and selling banana chips, employing five members. This is an example of:
e: Micro-enterprise development is a central component of the mission.

q: The principal reason Kudumbashree is described as a women's empowerment programme rather than only a credit scheme is that it:
o: Is funded by an international agency
Builds women's collectives that also participate in local planning and governance
e: The CDS network is linked to local self-government planning in Kerala.

q: Choose the correct objective of Balasabha.
o: Collectives of children of Kudumbashree families
Highly subsidised foodgrain for the poorest families
Gender help desk supporting women in distress
e: They promote learning, creativity and participation.

q: Which of the following describes Pradhan Mantri Matru Vandana Yojana correctly?
o: Hundred days of guaranteed wage employment to rural households
Skill training for rural youth to take up self-employment
Improving the child sex ratio and girls' education
Conditional cash benefit to pregnant and lactating mothers
e: It partly compensates for wage loss during pregnancy.

q: Select the statement that applies to Year the World Trade Organization was established.
e: It succeeded GATT after the Uruguay Round.

q: What is the main objective of Kudumbashree?
o: Clean cooking fuel connections to poor households
Poverty eradication and women's empowerment in Kerala
Gender help desk supporting women in distress
Highly subsidised foodgrain for the poorest families
e: It works through neighbourhood groups federated up to the local body.

q: PDS stands for:
e: The network of fair price shops distributing subsidised essentials.

q: 'Transfer of functions, funds and functionaries to local bodies' best describes which concept?
e: The 73rd and 74th Amendments gave it constitutional backing.

q: Select the statement that applies to Number of subjects in the Eleventh Schedule.
e: The Twelfth Schedule for municipalities lists 18 subjects.

q: Choose the correct statement about Jean Dreze.
o: Analysis of global cultural flows as scapes
Leadership of the Silent Valley movement in Kerala
Thesis of declining terms of trade for primary exporters
Collaborative work on hunger, public action and rights
e: He worked with Amartya Sen on India's development record.

q: Choose the correct objective of Poshan Abhiyaan.
o: Reduction of stunting, undernutrition and anaemia
Pensions and family benefit for the destitute
Livelihoods and shelter for the urban poor
Highly subsidised foodgrain for the poorest families
e: It uses convergence and technology-based monitoring.

q: Which item corresponds to 'Transboundary movement of hazardous wastes'?
e: It was adopted in 1989.

q: T.M. Thomas Isaac is remembered in this field for:
o: Analysis of global cultural flows as scapes
Founding of the Women in Development approach
Analysis of Kerala's decentralised People's Plan Campaign
Thesis that technology has flattened the world
e: He wrote on local democracy and participatory planning.

q: Which of the following is correct about Kudumbashree collective for children?
e: It promotes learning, creativity and participation among children.

q: Afforestation — which of the following is correct?
o: Planting of trees on land that was not previously forest
Physical and economic access to sufficient safe and nutritious food
Adaptation of global products and ideas to local conditions
Formal credit relationship between a self-help group and a bank
e: Reforestation restores cover on recently cleared land.

q: Year of the Paris Agreement — identify the correct association.
e: It was adopted at COP21 and entered into force in 2016.

q: In technical usage, 'Composting' denotes:
o: Shrinking of the experience of distance through technology
Emigration of highly skilled persons from poorer countries
Precipitation made acidic by sulphur and nitrogen oxides
Controlled aerobic decomposition of organic waste into manure
e: Vermicomposting uses earthworms to hasten the process.

q: Which contribution is associated with Raul Prebisch?
o: Thesis of declining terms of trade for primary exporters
Founding of the Women in Development approach
Exposure of ecological damage caused by pesticides
Analysis of empowerment as resources, agency and achievements
e: He led ECLA and became the first Secretary-General of UNCTAD.

q: 'Spread of a uniform global culture displacing local forms' best describes which concept?
e: Critics describe it as cultural imperialism.

q: The acronym IMF refers to:
e: Created at Bretton Woods to support exchange stability.

q: The acronym TPDS refers to:
e: Introduced in 1997 to focus subsidies on poor households.

q: In full, IBRD is:
o: International Bank for Reconstruction and Development
Training of Rural Youth for Self-Employment
e: The original institution of the World Bank Group.

q: 'Inability to meet the minimum requirements for survival' best describes which concept?
e: It is measured against a fixed subsistence standard.

q: Choose the correct option regarding State where Panchayati Raj was first inaugurated.
e: Nehru inaugurated it at Nagaur on 2 October 1959.

q: Select the full form corresponding to SEZ.
e: An enclave with special trade and tax rules to attract investment.

q: The correct answer regarding Date of Earth Day is:
e: It has been observed worldwide since 1970.

q: Which of the following is correct about Year of the Kyoto Protocol?
e: It entered into force in 2005.

q: 'Human Development Report of 1995' is associated with:
o: Greenhouse gas chiefly released by paddy fields and livestock
Report in which the GDI and GEM were introduced
Year of India's liberalisation, privatisation and globalisation reforms
Agency that publishes the India State of Forest Report
e: That report was devoted to gender and human development.

q: GEM stands for:
e: It measures women's participation in economic and political decision-making.

q: Kudumbashree programme for destitute families is:
e: It provides food, health, housing and livelihood support.

q: In technical usage, 'Globalisation' denotes:
o: Degradation of dry land into desert-like conditions
Region with exceptional endemic species under threat
Long-term shifts in temperature and weather patterns
Growing interconnection of economies, cultures and populations
e: It involves flows of goods, capital, people, technology and ideas.

q: Integrated Rural Development Programme is primarily meant for:
o: Self-employment assets for rural families below the poverty line
Self-employment of the rural poor through self-help groups
Skill training for rural youth to take up self-employment
Palliative and medical care for the elderly in Kerala
e: Subsidy and bank credit were combined for asset creation.

q: Identify the concept: Emigration of highly skilled persons from poorer countries
e: It may be offset partly by remittances and return migration.

q: Which term is defined as 'Engineered site for the disposal of residual waste'?
e: Liners and leachate collection protect groundwater.

q: Choose the correct statement about Arturo Escobar.
e: Development is analysed as a regime of representation.

q: The short form used for 'Development of Women and Children in Rural Areas' is:
e: A group-based programme for rural women launched in 1982.

q: The target group / purpose of Integrated Child Development Services is:
o: Institution building and livelihoods for rural poor women
Self-employment of the rural poor through self-help groups
Conditional cash benefit to pregnant and lactating mothers
Supplementary nutrition and pre-school education for young children
e: It also covers pregnant women and nursing mothers.

q: Identify the programme concerned with Self-employment for educated unemployed youth.
e: It provided subsidised credit for small ventures.

q: Choose the correct statement about Samir Amin.
o: Framework of gender planning and the triple role
Strategy of delinking from the world capitalist system
Analysis of community governance of common resources
Leadership of the Silent Valley movement in Kerala
e: He wrote on accumulation on a world scale.

q: The correct answer regarding Gas that leaked in the Bhopal disaster of 1984 is:
e: It escaped from the Union Carbide pesticide plant.

q: What is meant by 'Strategic gender needs'?
o: Needs arising from the wish to change subordinate positions
Small voluntary savings and credit group of poor members
Physical relocation of displaced households to a new site
Increasing concentration of a toxin along the food chain
e: Land rights, legal equality and political voice are examples.

q: Gender and Development — which of the following is correct?
o: Engineered site for the disposal of residual waste
Approach analysing unequal relations between women and men
Appraisal of likely environmental effects of a project
Resource replenished naturally within a human time scale
e: It targets the structures that produce subordination.

q: Forest cover target of the National Forest Policy of 1988 is best associated with:
o: Health, education and standard of living
e: Two-thirds is the target in hill and mountain regions.

q: Which term is defined as 'Planting of trees on land that was not previously forest'?
e: Reforestation restores cover on recently cleared land.

q: In full, NGT is:
e: Established in 2010 for speedy environmental adjudication.

q: Principle of waste management summarised as 3R — identify the correct association.
e: Reduction at source is preferred over recycling.

q: Thrift — which of the following is correct?
o: Regular small savings mobilised within a group
Region with exceptional endemic species under threat
Firm producing and selling across several countries
Unequal access to information and communication technology
e: It builds the corpus for internal lending.

q: Soil erosion refers to:
o: Unequal access to information and communication technology
Growing interconnection of economies, cultures and populations
Removal of topsoil by wind and water
Thinning of stratospheric ozone by halogenated chemicals
e: Loss of vegetation cover greatly accelerates it.

q: 'Neighbourhood Group' is abbreviated as:
e: The grassroots unit of Kudumbashree, also called ayalkoottam.

q: The acronym GII refers to:
e: Introduced in 2010 covering reproductive health, empowerment and labour market.

q: Which term is defined as 'Duty to leave a comparable resource base to future generations'?
e: It underlies the idea of sustainable development.

q: Subject of the Minamata Convention of 2013 is best associated with:
o: Control of mercury emissions and use
Tribal and other rural poor communities
e: It is named after the Japanese mercury poisoning disaster.

q: Select the full form corresponding to WTO.
e: Established in 1995 as the successor to GATT.

q: Which abbreviation denotes 'Environmental Impact Assessment'?
e: A mandatory appraisal for specified categories of projects.

q: DWCRA was launched mainly to:
o: Universal sanitation coverage and elimination of open defecation
Supplementary wage employment in the most backward districts
Group-based income generation for rural women and children
Skill training for rural youth to take up self-employment
e: It anticipated later self-help group programmes.

q: Norman Borlaug is remembered in this field for:
o: World-systems analysis of core and periphery
e: His work underpinned the global Green Revolution.

q: People's Plan Campaign was launched mainly to:
o: Decentralised participatory planning with devolved plan funds
Self-employment of the rural poor through self-help groups
Clean cooking fuel connections to poor households
Door-to-door waste collection by women's enterprise groups
e: It began in Kerala in 1996 during the Ninth Five Year Plan.

q: GATT is the abbreviated form of:
o: General Agreement on Tariffs and Trade
Convention on International Trade in Endangered Species
General Agreement on Trade in Services
e: Signed in 1947 and replaced by the WTO in 1995.

q: Which year is associated with the Land Acquisition Act?
e: The colonial statute long used for compulsory acquisition.

q: Identify the programme concerned with Hundred days of guaranteed wage employment to rural households.
e: Work must be provided within fifteen days of application.

q: Select the correct meaning of the term Rainwater harvesting.
o: Collection and storage of rainfall for later use
Resource replenished naturally within a human time scale
Controlled aerobic decomposition of organic waste into manure
Approach analysing unequal relations between women and men
e: It recharges aquifers and reduces dependence on piped supply.

q: Distance within which MGNREGS work should be provided — identify the correct association.
o: Health, education and standard of living
e: Beyond this an extra wage allowance is payable.

q: Under which scheme is 'Livelihoods and shelter for the urban poor' provided?
e: It supports urban SHGs, street vendors and skill training.

q: Scheduled Tribes and Other Traditional Forest Dwellers Forest Rights Act — the correct year is:
e: It recognises individual and community rights over forest land.

q: The correct answer regarding Date of World Environment Day is:
e: It marks the opening of the Stockholm Conference.

q: Which of the following relates to Principle of waste management summarised as 3R?
e: Reduction at source is preferred over recycling.

q: Under which scheme is 'Clean cooking fuel connections to poor households' provided?
e: It aims to reduce indoor air pollution and drudgery for women.

q: Which of the following best explains Decentralisation?
o: Transfer of functions, funds and functionaries to local bodies
Spread of a uniform global culture displacing local forms
Appraisal of the social consequences of a proposed project
Restoration of livelihoods and living standards of displaced people
e: The 73rd and 74th Amendments gave it constitutional backing.

q: Number of Sustainable Development Goals is best associated with:
e: They contain 169 targets under the 2030 Agenda.

q: Select the correct meaning of the term Biodiversity.
o: Unequal access to information and communication technology
Growing interconnection of economies, cultures and populations
Variety of living organisms and ecosystems
Small collateral-free loans to poor borrowers
e: It includes genetic, species and ecosystem diversity.

q: Which term is defined as 'Total greenhouse gases attributable to an activity or person'?
e: It is expressed in tonnes of carbon dioxide equivalent.

q: Pradhan Mantri Ujjwala Yojana is primarily meant for:
o: Clean cooking fuel connections to poor households
Highly subsidised foodgrain for the poorest families
Group-based income generation for rural women and children
Decentralised participatory planning with devolved plan funds
e: It aims to reduce indoor air pollution and drudgery for women.

q: Which of the following is correct about Subject of the Ramsar Convention?
e: It was signed in Iran in 1971.

q: Select the statement that applies to Report in which the GDI and GEM were introduced.
e: That report was devoted to gender and human development.

q: Identify the correct expansion of NFSA.
e: The 2013 law creating legal entitlements to subsidised foodgrain.

q: Right to Information Act — the correct year is:
e: It created a statutory right of access to public information.

q: Index that replaced the GDI and GEM in 2010 is:
e: It covers reproductive health, empowerment and the labour market.

q: Expand the abbreviation AAY.
e: Highly subsidised grain for the poorest families.

q: Wildlife Protection Act — the correct year is:
e: It provides for protected areas and schedules of protected species.

q: Immanuel Wallerstein is best known for:
o: Ecofeminist analysis of patriarchy and accumulation
World-systems analysis of core and periphery
Analysis of the global network society
e: A single capitalist world economy structures unequal exchange.

q: Identify the programme concerned with Group-based income generation for rural women and children.
e: It anticipated later self-help group programmes.

q: Select the full form corresponding to NSAP.
e: It provides pensions and family benefit to the poor.

q: Jean Dreze contributed to the discipline mainly through:
o: Analysis of global cultural flows as scapes
Collaborative work on hunger, public action and rights
Founding of the Women in Development approach
Analysis of empowerment as resources, agency and achievements
e: He worked with Amartya Sen on India's development record.

q: Expand the abbreviation IDA.
e: The soft-loan window of the World Bank for the poorest countries.

q: Annapurna Scheme is primarily meant for:
o: Hundred days of guaranteed wage employment to rural households
Housing assistance to rural below poverty line families
Institution building and livelihoods for rural poor women
Free foodgrain for destitute elderly not covered by pension
e: It supplements the old age pension programmes.

q: 'Controlled burning of waste at high temperature' best describes which concept?
e: It reduces volume but may release harmful emissions.

q: Sugathakumari is remembered in this field for:
o: Argument for independent land rights for women
Leadership of the Silent Valley movement in Kerala
Analysis of community governance of common resources
Collaborative work on hunger, public action and rights
e: The poet-activist campaigned against the hydel project.

q: The idea of 'Exposure of ecological damage caused by pesticides' was put forward by:
e: Silent Spring was published in 1962.
