e: Empowerment expands the ability to make strategic life choices.

q: Which of the following relates to Kudumbashree programme for destitute families?
e: It provides food, health, housing and livelihood support.

q: Who is associated with 'Organisation of Chipko through village cooperatives'?
e: He founded the Dasholi Gram Swarajya Sangh.

q: W.W. Rostow is best known for:
o: Leadership of the Narmada Bachao Andolan
Thesis of the development of underdevelopment
Analysis of the global network society
e: Modernisation proceeds from traditional society to mass consumption.

q: MGNREGS is primarily meant for:
o: Hundred days of guaranteed wage employment to rural households
Palliative and medical care for the elderly in Kerala
Supplementary nutrition and pre-school education for young children
Technical support for sanitation and waste management in Kerala
e: Work must be provided within fifteen days of application.

q: Remittance can be best understood as:
o: Region with exceptional endemic species under threat
Money sent home by migrants working elsewhere
Growing interconnection of economies, cultures and populations
Unequal access to information and communication technology
e: Remittances are a major part of Kerala's household economy.

q: Headquarters of the International Monetary Fund is:
e: The World Bank is also headquartered there.

q: Development-induced displacement — which of the following is correct?
o: Deprivation measured against prevailing living standards
Firm producing and selling across several countries
Maximum population an environment can support indefinitely
Forced resettlement caused by development projects
e: Dams, mines, highways and industrial zones are common causes.

q: Gender audit — which of the following is correct?
o: Systematic review of an organisation's gender performance
Degradation of dry land into desert-like conditions
Growing interconnection of economies, cultures and populations
Partnership of forest departments with village committees
e: It examines policy, staffing, culture, budgets and outcomes.

q: Who is associated with 'Critique of IMF conditionality in globalisation'?
e: Globalization and Its Discontents appeared in 2002.

q: The name Arturo Escobar is connected with:
o: Analysis of the global network society
Ecofeminist analysis of patriarchy and accumulation
Critique of IMF conditionality in globalisation
e: Development is analysed as a regime of representation.

q: 'Trade Related Aspects of Intellectual Property Rights' is abbreviated as:
e: A WTO agreement setting minimum standards of IP protection.

q: Whose work centres on 'Analysis of global cultural flows as scapes'?
e: Ethnoscapes, mediascapes, technoscapes, financescapes and ideoscapes.

q: Choose the correct option regarding Year the World Trade Organization was established.
e: It succeeded GATT after the Uruguay Round.

q: Date of World Water Day is best associated with:
e: It draws attention to freshwater management.

q: The short form used for 'National Rural Livelihoods Mission' is:
e: Also known as Aajeevika and later as DAY-NRLM.

q: Which of the following is correct about Committee that recommended a two-tier panchayat system in 1978?
e: It proposed mandal panchayats and zilla parishads.

q: Eligibility for membership of a Kudumbashree neighbourhood group is best associated with:
o: One adult woman from each family
e: Preference is given to women from risk families.

q: Project opposed by the Narmada Bachao Andolan is best associated with:
e: The movement began in the mid-1980s.

q: In full, GII is:
e: Introduced in 2010 covering reproductive health, empowerment and labour market.

q: The acronym PDS refers to:
e: The network of fair price shops distributing subsidised essentials.

q: Amartya Sen contributed to the discipline mainly through:
e: Development is the expansion of substantive human freedoms.

q: Which term is defined as 'Discarded solid material from households, institutions and industry'?
e: It is classified as biodegradable, recyclable and hazardous.

q: SEZ stands for:
e: An enclave with special trade and tax rules to attract investment.

q: Under which scheme is 'Improving the child sex ratio and girls' education' provided?
e: It was launched in 2015 in districts with adverse sex ratios.

q: Identify what is linked with Year of India's liberalisation, privatisation and globalisation reforms.
e: The New Economic Policy followed a balance of payments crisis.

q: Choose the correct statement about Raul Prebisch.
o: Leadership of the women of Reni village in Chipko
Strategy of delinking from the world capitalist system
Argument for independent land rights for women
Thesis of declining terms of trade for primary exporters
e: He led ECLA and became the first Secretary-General of UNCTAD.

q: Which year is associated with the Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition Act?
e: It replaced the Land Acquisition Act of 1894.

q: Manuel Castells is remembered in this field for:
o: World-systems analysis of core and periphery
Concept of circular and cumulative causation
Analysis of the global network society
e: Information flows reorganise economy, power and identity.

q: Under which scheme is 'Poverty eradication and women's empowerment in Kerala' provided?
e: It works through neighbourhood groups federated up to the local body.

q: 'Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change' is abbreviated as:
e: Set up in 1988 by WMO and UNEP to assess climate science.

q: In full, GDI is:
e: Introduced in the Human Development Report of 1995.

q: Who is associated with 'Concept of circular and cumulative causation'?
e: Asian Drama analysed obstacles to development in South Asia.

q: Choose the correct objective of Swarnajayanti Gram Swarozgar Yojana.
o: Conditional cash benefit to pregnant and lactating mothers
Supplementary wage employment in the most backward districts
Self-employment assets for rural families below the poverty line
Self-employment of the rural poor through self-help groups
e: It merged IRDP, TRYSEM, DWCRA and allied schemes.

q: The Dowry Prohibition Act was passed in the year:
e: The Dowry Prohibition Act, 1961 prohibits giving and taking of dowry.

q: Under the POCSO Act, 2012 a 'child' means a person below the age of:
e: Section 2(d) of POCSO defines a child as any person below eighteen years.

q: Which of the following Acts is gender neutral with respect to the victim?
o: Sexual Harassment of Women at Workplace Act
e: POCSO, 2012 protects all children irrespective of gender.

q: The Untouchability (Offences) Act, 1955 was renamed in 1976 as the:
e: The 1955 Act was renamed the Protection of Civil Rights Act with effect from 1976.

q: Untouchability is abolished by which Article of the Indian Constitution?
e: Article 17 abolishes untouchability and forbids its practice in any form.

q: The Narcotic Drugs and Psychotropic Substances Act belongs to the year:
e: The NDPS Act, 1985 is the principal anti-narcotics legislation in India.

q: The Pre-Natal Diagnostic Techniques (Regulation and Prevention of Misuse) Act was passed in:
e: The PNDT Act, 1994 was amended in 2003 and renamed the PCPNDT Act.

q: The Transgender Persons (Protection of Rights) Act was enacted in:
e: The Transgender Persons (Protection of Rights) Act, 2019 followed the NALSA judgment.

q: The Maintenance and Welfare of Parents and Senior Citizens Act was passed in:
e: The 2007 Act creates a summary maintenance remedy for parents and senior citizens.

q: Under the Maintenance and Welfare of Parents and Senior Citizens Act, 2007 a senior citizen is a person aged:
e: Section 2(h) defines a senior citizen as a citizen aged sixty years or above.

q: Which of the following is NOT a relief available under the PWDVA, 2005?
e: The PWDVA provides civil reliefs only; divorce is granted under personal or matrimonial law.

q: A woman aggrieved under the PWDVA, 2005 files her application before the:
e: Applications under Section 12 are filed before a Judicial Magistrate of the First Class.

q: Which functionary is specially created by the PWDVA, 2005?
e: The Act requires State Governments to appoint Protection Officers in every district.

q: Dowry death is dealt with under which section of the Indian Penal Code?
e: Section 304B IPC defines and punishes dowry death.

q: Cruelty to a married woman by her husband or his relatives is punishable under:
e: Section 498A IPC was inserted in 1983 to punish matrimonial cruelty.

q: A death is treated as a dowry death if it occurs within how many years of marriage?
e: Section 304B applies to unnatural death within seven years of marriage.

q: The minimum punishment for giving or taking dowry under the Dowry Prohibition Act is imprisonment of:
e: Section 3 prescribes imprisonment of not less than five years and fine.

q: Mandatory reporting of a sexual offence against a child is provided in which section of POCSO?
e: Section 19 of POCSO makes reporting of such offences compulsory for any person.

q: Under POCSO, the special court is expected to complete the trial ordinarily within:
e: Section 35 requires the Special Court to complete the trial within one year as far as possible.

q: Which body deals with a child in conflict with law under the JJ Act, 2015?
e: The Juvenile Justice Board handles children alleged to be in conflict with law.

q: A child in need of care and protection is produced before the:
e: The Child Welfare Committee is the authority for children in need of care and protection.

q: Under the JJ Act, 2015 a child aged 16 to 18 may be tried as an adult for:
e: Only heinous offences allow transfer after a preliminary assessment by the Board.

q: The nodal body for adoption in India is:
e: The Central Adoption Resource Authority regulates adoption under the JJ Act.

q: The National Commission for Women was constituted under an Act of the year:
e: The National Commission for Women Act, 1990 led to the Commission being set up in 1992.

q: The National Commission for Protection of Child Rights was set up under an Act of:
e: The Commissions for Protection of Child Rights Act, 2005 created the NCPCR in 2007.

q: The child helpline number in India is:
e: CHILDLINE 1098 is the round-the-clock emergency helpline for children.

q: The women helpline number in India is:
e: 181 is the national women helpline for women affected by violence.

q: The national helpline for senior citizens, Elderline, is:
e: Elderline 14567 is the toll-free helpline for senior citizens.

q: Which of the following is NOT one of Durkheim's types of suicide?
e: Durkheim described egoistic, altruistic, anomic and fatalistic suicide.

q: Suicide arising from excessive social regulation and blocked futures is termed:
e: Fatalistic suicide occurs under oppressive discipline, as among slaves or prisoners.

q: Durkheim's 'Suicide' was published in the year:
e: Le Suicide was published in 1897 and is a classic of empirical sociology.

q: Merton's strain theory explains deviance as a gap between:
e: Merton argued that deviance arises when legitimate means to cultural goals are blocked.

q: Which of Merton's modes of adaptation accepts goals but rejects legitimate means?
e: Innovation is the acceptance of success goals with illegitimate means.

q: Rejection of both cultural goals and institutional means, and their replacement with new ones, is called:
e: Rebellion seeks to substitute a new set of goals and means.

q: Differential association theory was proposed by:
e: Sutherland held that criminal behaviour is learned in intimate personal groups.

q: Labelling theory of deviance is associated with:
e: Becker's 'Outsiders' (1963) argued that deviance is created by societal reaction.

q: The distinction between primary and secondary deviance was drawn by:
e: Lemert described secondary deviance as deviance adopted after labelling.

q: The theory of the 'born criminal' was advanced by:
e: Lombroso's biological positivism proposed atavistic criminal types.

q: The concept of 'white collar crime' was introduced by:
e: Sutherland coined the term in 1939 for crime by persons of high social status.

q: Social bond or social control theory was developed by:
e: Hirschi listed attachment, commitment, involvement and belief as social bonds.

q: Which theory holds that delinquency arises in lower-class boys as a reaction to middle-class standards?
e: Albert Cohen's 'Delinquent Boys' (1955) explained status frustration.

q: 'Techniques of neutralisation' is associated with:
e: Sykes and Matza described rationalisations used by delinquents to justify acts.

q: Social disorganisation theory of crime emerged from the studies of:
e: Shaw and McKay of the Chicago School linked delinquency to zones of transition.

q: The concept of stigma as a 'spoiled identity' was developed by:
e: Goffman's 'Stigma' (1963) analysed discrediting attributes in social interaction.

q: The 'culture of poverty' thesis was put forward by:
e: Oscar Lewis developed the thesis from his studies of Mexican and Puerto Rican families.

q: The idea of the 'vicious circle of poverty' is associated with:
e: Nurkse described poverty as self-perpetuating through low income and low savings.

q: The capability approach to understanding poverty was developed by:
e: Sen defined poverty as deprivation of basic capabilities rather than low income.

q: The Human Development Index was devised principally by:
e: Mahbub ul Haq created the HDI for the first Human Development Report in 1990.

q: The Multidimensional Poverty Index measures deprivation in:
o: Health, education and standard of living
e: The global MPI uses three dimensions and ten indicators.

q: The Gini coefficient measures:
e: The Gini coefficient ranges from 0 (perfect equality) to 1 (perfect inequality).

q: The graphical device used to depict income inequality is the:
e: The Lorenz curve plots cumulative income against cumulative population.

q: The inverted-U relationship between economic growth and inequality is known as the:
e: Simon Kuznets suggested inequality first rises and then falls with development.

q: The calorie norms of 2400 in rural and 2100 in urban areas were fixed by the:
e: The Y. K. Alagh Task Force (1979) laid down these per capita daily calorie norms.

q: The Tendulkar Committee on poverty estimation submitted its report in:
e: The Suresh Tendulkar Committee reported in 2009 and revised the poverty line methodology.

q: The Rangarajan Committee on measurement of poverty reported in:
e: The C. Rangarajan Expert Group submitted its report in 2014.

q: Which of the following is an example of absolute poverty?
o: Owning fewer consumer goods than average
Inability to obtain minimum food, clothing and shelter
e: Absolute poverty is the failure to meet minimum subsistence requirements.

q: Disguised unemployment is most commonly found in:
e: Family farms often employ more persons than the work actually needs.

q: Unemployment caused by a mismatch between workers' skills and available jobs is:
e: Structural unemployment arises from changes in the structure of the economy.

q: Unemployment occurring during a downturn in the business cycle is termed:
e: Cyclical unemployment rises in recession and falls in boom.

q: The short period of joblessness while a worker moves between jobs is:
e: Frictional unemployment is transitional and usually short-lived.

q: Which type of unemployment is characteristic of the sugarcane and agricultural sectors?
e: Seasonal unemployment occurs in off-seasons of seasonal industries.

q: Kerala is particularly noted for a high level of:
e: High literacy with limited job creation has produced educated unemployment in Kerala.

q: MGNREGA guarantees wage employment for how many days in a financial year?
e: The Act guarantees 100 days of unskilled manual work per rural household.

q: Under MGNREGA, the minimum share of work to be given to women is:
e: At least one-third of beneficiaries must be women.

q: The Kudumbashree mission of Kerala was launched in the year:
e: Kudumbashree, the State Poverty Eradication Mission, was launched in 1998.

q: Which of the following is NOT a tier of the Kudumbashree three-tier structure?
e: Kudumbashree has NHGs, ADSs and CDSs; there is no District Development Society tier.

q: Severe acute malnutrition in a child aged 6 to 59 months is indicated by a MUAC below:
e: MUAC less than 11.5 cm indicates severe acute malnutrition.

q: Bilateral pitting oedema in a child indicates:
e: Nutritional bilateral pitting oedema is itself a criterion for SAM.

q: Low height for age in a child is termed:
e: Stunting reflects chronic undernutrition over a long period.

q: Low weight for height in a child is termed:
e: Wasting reflects acute recent weight loss or failure to gain weight.

q: The nutrient whose deficiency causes goitre is:
e: Iodine deficiency causes goitre and, in the foetus, cretinism.

q: Bitot's spots on the conjunctiva indicate deficiency of:
e: Bitot's spots are an early sign of xerophthalmia due to vitamin A deficiency.

q: Which vitamin deficiency causes the triad of dermatitis, diarrhoea and dementia?
e: Pellagra, caused by niacin deficiency, shows the classical three Ds.

q: Poshan Abhiyaan was launched in the year:
e: The National Nutrition Mission, Poshan Abhiyaan, was launched in March 2018.

q: Beti Bachao Beti Padhao was launched from which place?
e: The scheme was launched at Panipat, Haryana on 22 January 2015.

q: National Girl Child Day is observed in India on:
e: National Girl Child Day is observed on 24 January every year.

q: The International Day Against Drug Abuse and Illicit Trafficking is observed on:
e: 26 June is observed worldwide against drug abuse and illicit trafficking.

q: World Elder Abuse Awareness Day is observed on:
e: 15 June is observed as World Elder Abuse Awareness Day.

q: The UN Convention on the Rights of the Child was adopted in:
e: The CRC was adopted by the UN General Assembly in 1989; India ratified it in 1992.

q: CEDAW, the convention on elimination of discrimination against women, was adopted in:
e: CEDAW was adopted by the UN General Assembly in 1979.

q: The Vishaka Guidelines of 1997 dealt with:
e: The Supreme Court laid down binding guidelines later codified in the 2013 POSH Act.

q: Transgender persons were recognised as the third gender by the Supreme Court in:
e: NALSA v. Union of India (2014) recognised the third gender and self-identification.

q: Consensual homosexual acts between adults were decriminalised in:
o: Navtej Singh Johar v. Union of India
e: Navtej Singh Johar (2018) read down Section 377 IPC.

q: Under the Transgender Persons Act, 2019 a certificate of identity is issued by the:
e: Application for a certificate of identity is made to the District Magistrate.

q: The Vaikom Satyagraha of 1924-25 was directed against:
o: Denial of temple road access to lower castes
e: The satyagraha demanded the right to use roads around the Vaikom temple.

q: The Temple Entry Proclamation in Travancore was issued in:
e: The Temple Entry Proclamation was issued on 12 November 1936.

q: 'One caste, one religion, one God for man' was the message of:
e: This was the central teaching of Sree Narayana Guru.

q: The Kallumala agitation of 1915 was led by:
e: Ayyankali led the struggle against the compulsory stone-bead necklace for Dalit women.

q: 'Annihilation of Caste' was written by:
e: Ambedkar wrote 'Annihilation of Caste' as an undelivered address in 1936.

q: The Satyashodhak Samaj was founded by:
e: Jyotirao Phule founded the Satyashodhak Samaj in 1873.

q: Which of the following is NOT a feature of communalism?
o: Belief that religion defines the political community
Equal respect for all faiths by the state
Use of religious identity for political mobilisation
e: Equal respect for all faiths is secularism, the opposite of communalism.

q: Which Article of the Constitution protects the right of minorities to establish educational institutions?
e: Article 30 grants minorities the right to establish and administer educational institutions.

q: The Sachar Committee reported on the condition of:
e: The Sachar Committee (2006) studied the social and economic status of Muslims.

q: The Mandal Commission report dealt with reservation for:
e: The Mandal Commission (1980) recommended 27 per cent reservation for OBCs.

q: The ceiling of 50 per cent on total reservation was laid down in:
e: Indra Sawhney v. Union of India (1992) fixed the fifty per cent limit.

q: Which of the following is NOT a form of domestic violence under the PWDVA, 2005?
e: The Act covers physical, sexual, verbal, emotional and economic abuse.

q: An Internal Complaints Committee under the POSH Act, 2013 is mandatory in workplaces with:
e: Every workplace with ten or more workers must constitute an ICC.

q: A complaint of sexual harassment under the POSH Act must ordinarily be made within:
e: The limitation is three months from the incident, extendable by three more months.

q: The sex ratio of India according to Census 2011 is:
e: Census 2011 recorded 943 females per 1000 males in India.

q: The child sex ratio (0-6 years) in Census 2011 was:
e: The 0-6 child sex ratio in 2011 was 919 girls per 1000 boys.

q: Kerala's sex ratio according to Census 2011 is:
e: Kerala recorded 1084 females per 1000 males, the highest among states.

q: Which district of Kerala recorded the lowest sex ratio in Census 2011?
e: Idukki recorded the lowest sex ratio in Kerala in 2011.

q: Which of the following is NOT prohibited by the PCPNDT Act?
o: Communicating the sex of the foetus
e: Diagnostic ultrasound for medical purposes is permitted; sex disclosure is not.

q: A 4-year-old boy is brought to an Anganwadi with severe wasting, visible ribs, an old man's face and no oedema. The likely condition is:
e: Severe wasting without oedema is the classical picture of marasmus.

q: A 2-year-old presents with bilateral pitting oedema of the feet, flaky paint dermatosis and a moon face. This suggests:
e: Oedema with skin changes and moon face indicates kwashiorkor.

q: An Anganwadi worker measures a MUAC of 10.8 cm in a 3-year-old. Her correct action is to:
o: Refer the child as a case of severe acute malnutrition
Wait for three months and re-measure
e: MUAC below 11.5 cm is severe acute malnutrition and needs referral.

q: A pregnant woman is given iron and folic acid tablets chiefly to prevent:
e: IFA supplementation prevents nutritional anaemia in pregnancy.

q: A woman is beaten and driven out of her matrimonial home for not bringing a car. The immediate civil relief she may seek is:
o: Compensation under the Motor Vehicles Act
Protection and residence orders under the PWDVA
e: Sections 18 and 19 of the PWDVA provide protection and residence orders.

q: A school teacher notices unexplained injuries and withdrawal in a nine-year-old girl and suspects sexual abuse. Under POCSO she must:
o: Wait for the parents to complain
Counsel the child privately and keep it confidential
Report the matter to the police or the Special Juvenile Police Unit
e: Section 19 of POCSO makes reporting mandatory; failure is punishable under Section 21.

q: A 16-year-old boy is apprehended for committing theft. He must be produced before the:
e: A child in conflict with law is produced before the Juvenile Justice Board.

q: A six-year-old found begging alone at a railway station is best described as a:
o: Child in need of care and protection
e: Such a child is produced before the Child Welfare Committee under the JJ Act.

q: A scan centre discloses the sex of a foetus to the parents. This violates the:
e: Disclosure of the sex of the foetus is an offence under the PCPNDT Act.

q: A man refuses to maintain his 70-year-old mother. She may approach the:
o: Maintenance Tribunal under the Senior Citizens Act, 2007
e: The 2007 Act provides a summary remedy before a Maintenance Tribunal.

q: A chronic drinker stops alcohol abruptly and develops tremor, confusion and vivid hallucinations after two days. This is:
e: Delirium tremens is a severe alcohol withdrawal state and a medical emergency.

q: A chronic alcoholic shows severe memory loss and fills gaps with invented stories. This is:
e: Confabulation with amnesia is characteristic of Korsakoff syndrome.

q: Five members of a family work on a plot that three can easily manage. This illustrates:
e: The marginal productivity of the extra workers is nearly zero.

q: A shopkeeper who has finished his degree refuses low-skilled jobs and waits for a clerical post. This is an instance of:
e: Educated unemployment is a mismatch of aspiration, qualification and available work.

q: 'National Sample Survey Office' is abbreviated as:
e: Conducts surveys on employment and consumption.

q: Which of the following relates to First Juvenile Justice Act of India?
e: It was replaced in 2000 and again in 2015.

q: In which year was the Mental Healthcare Act enacted?
e: Replaced the Mental Health Act of 1987 and decriminalised attempted suicide.

q: Identify the correct expansion of NCSC.
e: Constitutional body under Article 338.

q: Marasmus is caused by the deficiency of:
e: The child shows severe wasting without oedema.

q: Hindu Marriage Act — the correct year is:
e: Codified Hindu marriage law including conditions of marriage.

q: Deficiency of Energy and protein together causes:
e: The child shows severe wasting without oedema.

q: 'Fifty per cent ceiling on total reservation' refers to:
e: It was delivered by the Supreme Court in 1992.

q: Fatalistic suicide — which of the following is correct?
o: Deprivation of financial resources within a domestic relationship
Condition widely regarded as undesirable and remediable
Process of improving participation of disadvantaged groups
Suicide under excessive regulation and blocked futures
e: Durkheim illustrated it with slaves and prisoners.

q: Which of the following best explains Recidivism?
o: Joblessness among qualified and schooled youth
Relapse into criminal behaviour after punishment
Deficiency of micronutrients without obvious hunger
Temporary joblessness while moving between jobs
e: A key measure of the failure of correction.

q: Select the correct description of Beriberi.
o: Bleeding gums and poor wound healing
e: Wet beriberi affects the heart and dry beriberi the nerves.

q: AWW stands for:
e: Frontline functionary of the ICDS at the village level.

q: Delayed clotting and haemorrhagic disease of the newborn indicates a shortage of:
e: A single dose at birth prevents newborn bleeding.

q: Which is the key feature of Foetal alcohol syndrome?
o: Facial anomalies and growth deficiency in the newborn
Reddened eyes, altered time sense and increased appetite
Severe wasting with an old man's face and no oedema
Visible enlargement of the thyroid gland
e: It results from maternal drinking during pregnancy.

q: Beriberi indicates a shortage of:
e: Vitamin B1 deficiency affects nerves and the heart.

q: Which of the following was enacted in 2017?
e: Replaced the Mental Health Act of 1987 and decriminalised attempted suicide.

q: The scheme meant for 'Highly subsidised foodgrains to the poorest households' is:
e: Each eligible household gets thirty-five kilograms a month.

q: Identify what is linked with Calorie norm fixed for rural India in 1979.
o: Equality of opportunity in public employment
First Backward Classes Commission of India
e: The urban norm was fixed at 2100 calories.

q: Article 15 is best associated with:
o: Petition of 1896 for the civil rights of the Ezhava community
Prohibition of employment of children below fourteen in hazardous work
Prohibition of discrimination on grounds of religion, race, caste, sex or birthplace
Prohibition of traffic in human beings and forced labour
e: Clause (3) permits special provision for women and children.

q: Which item corresponds to 'Petition of 1896 for the civil rights of the Ezhava community'?
e: It was led by Dr Palpu.

q: Under which scheme is 'Child protection services and care of vulnerable children' provided?
e: It subsumes the earlier Integrated Child Protection Scheme.

q: In full, SHG is:
e: Small savings and credit group, usually of women.

q: 'Recognition of transgender persons as the third gender' refers to:
e: Delivered by the Supreme Court in 2014.

q: The legislation of the year 1850 referred to here is:
e: Protected converts and outcastes from loss of property rights.

q: The focus of PM POSHAN is:
o: Shelter and rehabilitation for women in difficult circumstances
Free foodgrains to uncovered destitute elderly persons
Cash assistance to promote institutional delivery
Hot cooked midday meal for school children
e: The renamed national midday meal scheme.

q: 'Juvenile Delinquency and Urban Areas' was written by:
e: It mapped delinquency across Chicago's zones.

q: Choose the correct definition of Anomic suicide.
o: Suicide arising from weak integration with social groups
Proportion of population living below the poverty line
Suicide resulting from sudden disruption of social regulation
Concentration of a community in segregated residential areas
e: It rises during economic booms as well as crises.

q: The short form used for 'Prevention of Sexual Harassment' is:
e: Popular name of the workplace sexual harassment law of 2013.

q: Identify the programme concerned with Conditional maternity benefit to pregnant and lactating women.
e: It partly compensates wage loss during pregnancy.

q: Select the statement that applies to Composition of the Juvenile Justice Board.
o: Cruelty to a married woman by husband or his relatives
Recommendations on criminal law relating to offences against women
Duty of the State to prohibit intoxicating drinks and drugs
A magistrate and two social workers including one woman
e: The magistrate acts as the principal magistrate.

q: 'Child Development Project Officer' is abbreviated as:
e: Officer in charge of an ICDS project block.

q: Ragnar Nurkse is remembered in this field for:
e: Low income causes low savings which in turn perpetuate low income.

q: The concept described as 'Harm caused by unequal social structures rather than direct assault' is called:
e: Concept developed by Johan Galtung.

q: Swadhar Greh was launched mainly to:
o: Educational assistance to orphaned children living with relatives
Prevention of trafficking and rehabilitation of victims
Shelter and rehabilitation for women in difficult circumstances
Umbrella scheme for the welfare of senior citizens
e: It supports widows, destitute and trafficked women.

q: Which of the following is correct about Tele-MANAS mental health helpline?
e: It provides tele-counselling for mental health support.

q: The acronym ORS refers to:
e: Standard treatment for dehydration in diarrhoea.

q: Annapurna Scheme was launched mainly to:
o: Conditional maternity benefit to pregnant and lactating women
Child protection services and care of vulnerable children
Financial assistance to caregivers of bedridden patients
Free foodgrains to uncovered destitute elderly persons
e: It covers elderly persons not receiving old age pension.

q: 'National Crime Records Bureau' refers to:
o: Body that compiles Crime in India
Composition of the Child Welfare Committee
Year of the first Human Development Report
e: It publishes annual crime statistics for the country.

q: Underweight — which of the following is correct?
o: Number of females per thousand males
Law-breaking behaviour by persons below eighteen
Deficiency of micronutrients without obvious hunger
e: A composite indicator of acute and chronic undernutrition.

q: Nirbhaya Fund was launched mainly to:
o: Financing of projects for the safety and security of women
Free cooking gas connections to women of poor households
Shelter and rehabilitation for women in difficult circumstances
Child protection services and care of vulnerable children
e: Created in 2013 after the Delhi gang rape.

q: 'Indira Gandhi National Widow Pension Scheme' is abbreviated as:
e: Pension for widows below the poverty line.

Right of minorities to establish educational institutions
Mandatory reporting of sexual offences against children
Protection order restraining acts of domestic violence
e: Failure to report is punishable under Section 21.

q: Choose the correct statement about Howard Becker.
e: Deviance is created by the rules and reactions of society.

q: Juvenile Justice (Care and Protection of Children) Act is a legislation of the year:
e: Current law on children in conflict with law and in need of care.

q: 'Eighteen years' refers to:
o: Agencies that publish the global Multidimensional Poverty Index
Entitlement of a priority household under the National Food Security Act
Minimum legal age of marriage for women in India
Year of the first Human Development Report
e: Fixed by the Prohibition of Child Marriage Act, 2006.

q: Identify the year of the Factories Act.
e: Regulates working conditions and prohibits child employment in factories.

q: What is meant by 'Elder abuse'?
o: Harm or distress caused to an older person by a person in a position of trust
Person whose gender identity differs from the sex assigned at birth
Systematic denial of participation, resources and rights to a group
Distressing signs appearing when a dependent person stops the substance
e: It includes neglect, financial exploitation and abandonment.

q: The writer of 'Caste, Class and Power' is:
e: A study of changing stratification in a Tanjore village.

q: Lack of Vitamin C in the diet results in:
e: It presents with bleeding gums and poor wound healing.

q: Which abbreviation denotes 'National Commission for Protection of Child Rights'?
e: Constituted in 2007 under the CPCR Act, 2005.

q: Minimum legal age of marriage for men in India is:
e: Marriage below this age is a punishable offence.

q: Which year is associated with the Untouchability (Offences) Act?
e: First law penalising untouchability; renamed PCR Act in 1976.

q: Which scheme aims at Umbrella scheme for the welfare of senior citizens?
e: It consolidates elderly welfare programmes of the centre.

q: Which condition results from insufficient Vitamin A?
e: Bitot's spots are an early sign of the deficiency.

q: Which scheme aims at Housing for the landless and homeless in Kerala?
e: It aims at complete housing security in the state.

q: Delirium tremens typically presents with:
o: Persistent inadequate weight gain in early childhood
Confusion, ataxia and eye movement paralysis
Tremor, confusion and hallucinations on alcohol withdrawal
e: It usually appears two to four days after stopping.

q: Identify the programme concerned with De-addiction and anti-drug campaign in Kerala.
e: Run by the Kerala State Excise Department.

q: Which of the following relates to Minimum legal age of marriage for women in India?
e: Fixed by the Prohibition of Child Marriage Act, 2006.

q: Which is the key feature of Goitre?
o: Bitot's spots and dryness of the conjunctiva
Subdural and retinal haemorrhage in an infant
Learned helplessness in a chronically abused woman
Visible enlargement of the thyroid gland
e: It is the commonest sign of iodine deficiency.

q: The target group / purpose of Nasha Mukt Bharat Abhiyaan is:
o: Mass campaign against drug and substance abuse
Child protection services and care of vulnerable children
Financial assistance to caregivers of bedridden patients
Highly subsidised foodgrains to the poorest households
e: It combines awareness, treatment and community outreach.

q: 'Residence order securing the shared household' refers to:
e: A woman cannot be evicted from the shared household.

q: In technical usage, 'Head count ratio' denotes:
o: Proportion of population living below the poverty line
Deprivation of financial resources within a domestic relationship
Joblessness from mismatch between skills and available jobs
Suicide arising from weak integration with social groups
e: It counts the poor but ignores the depth of poverty.

q: Identify the programme concerned with Health insurance cover to poor and vulnerable families.
e: It provides cashless secondary and tertiary care.

q: Rights of Persons with Disabilities Act received assent in the year:
e: Expanded recognised disabilities from seven to twenty-one.

q: Identify the correct expansion of NCPCR.
o: Indira Gandhi National Disability Pension Scheme
National Commission for Protection of Child Rights
e: Constituted in 2007 under the CPCR Act, 2005.

q: Identify the deficiency condition associated with Vitamin C.
e: It presents with bleeding gums and poor wound healing.

q: Which of the following describes Deendayal Antyodaya Yojana correctly?
o: Nutrition and life skills for out-of-school adolescent girls
Promotion of self help groups and sustainable livelihoods
Educational assistance to orphaned children living with relatives
Umbrella scheme for the welfare of senior citizens
e: It covers both rural and urban livelihood missions.

q: Section 498A IPC — identify the correct association.
o: A chairperson and four members with at least one woman
Prohibition of employment of children below fourteen in hazardous work
Cruelty to a married woman by husband or his relatives
Recommendations on criminal law relating to offences against women
e: Inserted in 1983 to deal with matrimonial cruelty.

q: Marginalisation can be best understood as:
o: Harm caused by unequal social structures rather than direct assault
Consumption of a large quantity of alcohol on one occasion
Person whose gender identity differs from the sex assigned at birth
Pushing of a group to the edge of social and economic life
e: It restricts voice, resources and opportunity.

q: Expand the abbreviation TPDS.
e: Food subsidy system targeting identified poor households.

q: In technical usage, 'Female infanticide' denotes:
o: Suicide under excessive regulation and blocked futures
Killing of a female infant after birth
Deprivation of financial resources within a domestic relationship
Minimum expenditure needed to meet basic needs
e: A historic practice reflecting strong son preference.

q: Which term is defined as 'Low weight for height'?
e: An indicator of acute undernutrition.

q: Select the statement that applies to Section 19 of POCSO.
o: Mandatory reporting of sexual offences against children
Equality of opportunity in public employment
Presumption of guilt of the accused
Freedom of conscience and free profession of religion
e: Failure to report is punishable under Section 21.

q: Ishwar Chandra Vidyasagar is remembered in this field for:
e: His work led to the Hindu Widows Remarriage Act of 1856.

q: Choose the correct option regarding Article 46.
o: A magistrate and two social workers including one woman
UNDP and the Oxford Poverty and Human Development Initiative
Promotion of educational and economic interests of weaker sections
Protest of 1915 against the compulsory stone bead necklace
e: It directs protection from social injustice and exploitation.

q: 'Definition of rape' is associated with:
e: It was substantially widened by the 2013 amendment.

q: The main symptom of Goitre is:
o: Visible enlargement of the thyroid gland
Scarring and shrinkage of the liver
Tremor, confusion and hallucinations on alcohol withdrawal
Subdural and retinal haemorrhage in an infant
e: It is the commonest sign of iodine deficiency.

q: CDPO — choose the correct expansion.
e: Officer in charge of an ICDS project block.

q: Transgender Persons (Protection of Rights) Act is a legislation of the year:
e: Prohibits discrimination and provides identity certificates.

q: Which of the following ideas is credited to Irawati Karve?
o: Expert group on state-wise poverty lines
Struggle for Dalit rights in Travancore
Movement for the annihilation of caste
Study of kinship organisation in India
e: She mapped regional patterns of Indian kinship.

q: The hallmark of Marasmus is:
o: Severe wasting with an old man's face and no oedema
Persistent inadequate weight gain in early childhood
Flashbacks and avoidance after a traumatic event
Stunted growth with intellectual disability from foetal iodine lack
e: It results from prolonged deficiency of energy and protein.

q: Albert Cohen contributed to the discipline mainly through:
e: Status frustration among working class boys generates gang subcultures.

q: Which abbreviation denotes 'National Commission for Scheduled Tribes'?
e: Constitutional body under Article 338A.

q: World No Tobacco Day — identify the correct association.
e: It highlights the health risks of tobacco use.

q: Deficiency of Riboflavin causes:
e: Vitamin B2 deficiency shows at the angles of the mouth.

q: Identify the deficiency condition associated with Folic acid.
o: Convulsions in infants and peripheral neuropathy
Megaloblastic anaemia and neural tube defects
e: Supplementation before conception prevents spina bifida.

q: Which item corresponds to 'Inter-dining organised to break caste commensality rules'?
e: It was promoted by Sahodaran Ayyappan.

q: SAM is the abbreviated form of:
e: Weight for height below minus three SD or MUAC under 11.5 cm.

q: The Unlawful Activities (Prevention) Act was passed by the legislature in:
e: Deals with unlawful associations and terrorist activities.

q: Choose the correct statement about Erving Goffman.
o: Expert group on state-wise poverty lines
Distinction between primary and secondary deviance
Concept of stigma and spoiled identity
Construction of the Human Development Index
e: Stigma discredits a person in the course of social interaction.

q: The correct answer regarding Article 25 is:
o: Prohibition of traffic in human beings and forced labour
Freedom of conscience and free profession of religion
Recognition of transgender persons as the third gender
Five kilograms of foodgrain per person per month
e: It is subject to public order, morality and health.

q: The Maternity Benefit Act belongs to which year?
e: Provides paid maternity leave to women employees.

q: NRC is the abbreviated form of:
e: Facility for inpatient management of severe acute malnutrition.

q: Korsakoff syndrome is characterised by:
o: Visible enlargement of the thyroid gland
e: It follows untreated thiamine deficiency in alcoholism.

q: 'Socially constructed roles and expectations attached to sex' best describes which concept?
e: Gender varies across cultures whereas sex is biological.

q: Culture of poverty refers to:
o: Deficiency, excess or imbalance in a person's intake of nutrients
Group that is numerically smaller and non-dominant in a society
Set of values said to be transmitted among the poor
Ideology that religious identity is the basis of political community
e: Advanced by Oscar Lewis and widely criticised as blaming the poor.

q: The writer of 'Homo Hierarchicus' is:
e: It interpreted caste through purity and pollution.

q: Identify the programme concerned with Bank loans to Scheduled Caste, Scheduled Tribe and women entrepreneurs.
e: Each bank branch is to finance such borrowers.

q: Which of the following is seen in Cretinism?
o: Reddened eyes, altered time sense and increased appetite
Flashbacks and avoidance after a traumatic event
Stunted growth with intellectual disability from foetal iodine lack
Scarring and shrinkage of the liver
e: It is prevented by iodine sufficiency in pregnancy.

q: Choose the correct option regarding Composition of the Juvenile Justice Board.
o: Prohibition of employment of children below fourteen in hazardous work
A magistrate and two social workers including one woman
Report on the social and economic status of Muslims
Free and compulsory education for children aged six to fourteen
e: The magistrate acts as the principal magistrate.

q: Which abbreviation denotes 'United Nations Children's Fund'?
e: UN agency for the welfare of children.

q: Which of the following ideas is credited to Frank Tannenbaum?
e: Public tagging of a young offender hardens a deviant identity.

q: Research undertaken to gain familiarity with a phenomenon about which little is known is called:
e: Exploratory or formulative research develops insights and sharpens the problem.

q: Research that answers the question 'why' by establishing cause and effect is:
e: Explanatory or causal research tests relationships between variables.

q: A survey describing the age, education and income of Anganwadi workers is an example of:
e: Descriptive research portrays the characteristics of a group accurately.

q: Research aimed at adding to the general body of knowledge without immediate use is:
e: Basic or fundamental research seeks theory building rather than application.

q: Research undertaken to solve an immediate practical problem is called:
e: Applied research is directed at a specific practical decision or problem.

q: Action research is chiefly credited to:
e: Kurt Lewin introduced action research in the 1940s as research leading to action.

q: The essential feature of participatory research is that:
o: The community takes part in defining and conducting the study
e: Participatory research treats the community as a partner rather than a subject.

q: Which approach relies mainly on numerical measurement and statistical analysis?
e: Quantitative research emphasises measurement, sampling and statistical inference.

q: Which of the following is NOT a qualitative method?
e: A structured questionnaire survey is a quantitative technique.

q: The deliberate combination of quantitative and qualitative approaches in one study is:
e: Mixed methods research integrates both approaches to strengthen inference.

q: Studying a population at a single point in time is a:
e: A cross-sectional study is a snapshot at one point in time.

q: A study that follows the same set of respondents over several years is a:
e: A panel study repeatedly measures the same individuals over time.

q: A study comparing successive samples from the same population at different times is a:
e: Trend studies use different samples of the same population over time.

q: A study of persons sharing a common experience within a defined period is a:
e: A cohort shares an event such as year of birth or year of marriage.

q: The intensive study of a single unit in its totality is called:
e: The case study gives depth rather than breadth of information.

q: The case study method in sociology was pioneered by:
e: Le Play's family monographs are regarded as early case studies.

q: Which of the following is a limitation of the case study method?
o: Its findings cannot be easily generalised
It permits the study of process
e: A single case limits statistical generalisation to the wider population.

q: Data collected by the investigator for the first time are called:
e: Primary data are original and collected directly from the field.

q: Census reports and NFHS data used by another researcher are:
e: Data already collected by someone else are secondary for the new user.

q: Which of the following is NOT an advantage of secondary data?
o: Always exactly suited to the research problem
e: Secondary data are collected for other purposes and may not fit the study.

q: The first step in the process of social research is:
e: The research process begins with selecting and defining the problem.

q: A small scale trial of the research instrument before the main study is called:
e: A pilot study reveals defects in the tool and the procedure.

q: The review of literature in a research project mainly helps to:
o: Increase the length of the report
Avoid duplication and sharpen the problem
e: The literature review locates the study within existing knowledge.

q: A tentative statement about the relationship between two or more variables is a:
e: A hypothesis is a testable proposition awaiting empirical verification.

q: The hypothesis of no difference or no relationship is called the:
e: The null hypothesis is the statement actually tested statistically.

q: A hypothesis stating that group A will score higher than group B is:
e: A directional hypothesis predicts the direction of the difference.

q: Which of the following is NOT a characteristic of a good hypothesis?
o: It should be clear and specific
It should be untestable and abstract
It should be related to a body of theory
e: An untestable statement cannot serve as a hypothesis.

q: The variable that is manipulated by the researcher is the:
e: The independent variable is the presumed cause.

q: The variable whose change is measured as an effect is the:
e: The dependent variable is the presumed effect.

q: A variable that lies between cause and effect and helps explain the link is:
e: An intervening variable mediates the relationship between two variables.

q: A variable not part of the study but capable of affecting the result is:
e: Extraneous variables threaten internal validity if uncontrolled.

q: A variable that can take only whole number values is:
e: Number of children in a family is a discrete variable.

q: In which sampling method does every unit of the population have a known and equal chance of selection?
e: Simple random sampling gives every unit an equal probability of selection.

q: Selecting every tenth name from a list of households is:
e: Systematic sampling uses a fixed sampling interval after a random start.

q: Dividing the population into homogeneous sub-groups before random selection is:
e: Stratified sampling improves representation of each sub-group.

q: Selecting whole villages at random and studying every household in them is:
e: In cluster sampling naturally occurring groups become the sampling unit.

q: Sampling in which existing respondents refer further respondents is:
e: Snowball sampling is useful for hidden or hard-to-reach populations.

q: Interviewing the first fifty persons who pass a street corner is:
e: Accidental or convenience sampling uses whoever is readily available.

q: Fixing the number of respondents to be drawn from each category in advance, without random selection, is:
e: Quota sampling resembles stratified sampling but selection is non-random.

q: The complete list of all units of a population from which a sample is drawn is the:
e: The sampling frame operationalises the population for selection.

q: The difference between a sample value and the true population value is:
e: Sampling error decreases as sample size increases.

q: A characteristic of the whole population, such as the population mean, is called a:
e: A value computed from a sample is a statistic; from a population a parameter.

q: A set of questions mailed to respondents to be filled in by themselves is a:
e: The questionnaire is self-administered while the schedule is filled by the investigator.

q: Which tool is best suited for studying illiterate respondents?
e: The interview schedule is filled by the trained investigator during interaction.

q: Observation in which the researcher takes part in the life of the group studied is:
e: Participant observation was developed notably by Bronislaw Malinowski.

q: Which of the following is a demerit of participant observation?
o: It suits the study of small groups
e: Deep involvement risks subjectivity and going native.

q: An interview with a predetermined fixed set of questions in a fixed order is:
e: Structured interviews allow comparability across respondents.

q: The technique of studying interpersonal choices and rejections within a group is:
e: Sociometry was developed by J. L. Moreno and uses the sociogram.

q: Systematic and objective analysis of the content of documents and media is called:
e: Content analysis converts qualitative material into quantitative categories.

q: The social distance scale was constructed by:
e: The Bogardus scale measures willingness to accept social contact with groups.

q: The five point agree-disagree summated rating scale is named after:
e: The Likert scale sums responses to a set of attitude statements.

q: The scalogram or cumulative scaling technique is associated with:
e: Guttman scaling assumes items form a cumulative unidimensional order.

q: The semantic differential scale using bipolar adjectives was developed by:
e: Osgood's scale rates concepts between opposite adjective pairs.

q: The method of equal appearing intervals in attitude scaling is credited to:
e: Thurstone used judges to place statements on an equal interval continuum.

q: Which scale of measurement only classifies without any order?
e: Nominal scales merely label categories such as religion or sex.

q: Ranking of students as first, second and third uses which scale?
e: Ordinal scales give order but not equal distances between ranks.

q: Temperature measured in degrees Celsius is an example of which scale?
e: Interval scales have equal intervals but an arbitrary zero.

q: Which scale of measurement has a true and absolute zero point?
e: Height, weight and income are ratio scale variables.

q: The consistency of a measuring instrument over repeated use is called:
e: A reliable tool gives consistent results under similar conditions.

q: The extent to which a test measures what it claims to measure is:
e: Validity concerns accuracy rather than consistency.

q: Administering the same test twice to the same group to check consistency gives:
e: The correlation between the two administrations is the reliability coefficient.

q: The coefficient commonly reported for internal consistency of a scale is:
e: Cronbach's alpha summarises inter-item consistency.

q: Validity judged by expert opinion on whether items cover the full domain is:
e: Content validity concerns adequate sampling of the domain of interest.

q: Which of the following statements about reliability and validity is correct?
o: A valid test must be reliable
A valid test is always unreliable
A reliable test is always valid
e: Reliability is necessary but not sufficient for validity.

q: The arithmetic mean of 4, 6, 8, 10 and 12 is:
e: The sum is 40 and dividing by 5 gives a mean of 8.

q: The median of the values 3, 7, 9, 15 and 21 is:
e: With five ordered values the third value, 9, is the median.

q: The mode of the series 2, 3, 3, 5, 7, 3, 8 is:
e: The value 3 occurs most frequently in the series.

q: Which measure of central tendency is most affected by extreme values?
e: The arithmetic mean is pulled towards outliers.

q: Which average is the only one that can be used for nominal data?
e: Only the mode can be computed for purely categorical data.

q: The range of the series 12, 18, 25, 30 and 42 is:
e: Range is the highest value minus the lowest, that is 42 minus 12.

q: The square of the standard deviation is called the:
e: Variance is the mean of the squared deviations from the mean.

q: Which measure of dispersion is considered the most reliable?
e: The standard deviation uses every observation and has useful properties.

q: The relative measure used to compare variability of two different series is:
e: The coefficient of variation expresses the SD as a percentage of the mean.

q: In a perfectly normal distribution, mean, median and mode are:
e: The normal curve is symmetrical so the three averages coincide.

q: The shape of the normal distribution curve is:
e: The normal curve is symmetrical, bell shaped and asymptotic.

q: In a normal distribution the percentage of cases falling within one standard deviation of the mean is about:
e: Roughly 68.26 per cent of cases lie within plus or minus one SD.

q: About what percentage of cases lie within two standard deviations of the mean in a normal curve?
e: Approximately 95.44 per cent of observations fall within two SDs.

q: The value of the correlation coefficient always lies between:
e: Pearson's r ranges from minus one to plus one inclusive.

q: A correlation coefficient of minus 0.90 indicates:
e: The sign shows direction and the magnitude shows strength.

q: The product moment coefficient of correlation was developed by:
e: Pearson's r is used for interval and ratio level data.

q: The rank order method of correlation is associated with:
e: Spearman's rho is used when data are in ranks.

q: Which statistical test is used to study association between two categorical variables?
e: The chi-square test compares observed and expected frequencies.

q: The chi-square test was developed by:
e: Karl Pearson introduced the chi-square goodness of fit test in 1900.

q: The Student's t-test was developed by:
e: Gosset published under the pen name 'Student' in 1908.

q: The t-test is most appropriate when:
o: Sample size is large and variance known
Sample size is small and population variance unknown
There are more than three groups
e: The t distribution corrects for the uncertainty of small samples.

q: Analysis of variance for comparing more than two group means was developed by:
e: Fisher developed ANOVA and the F ratio in agricultural experiments.

q: For a two by three contingency table the degrees of freedom for chi-square are:
e: Degrees of freedom equal (rows minus 1) times (columns minus 1), that is 1 times 2.

q: Rejecting a true null hypothesis is known as:
e: Type I error is the false rejection of a correct null hypothesis.

q: Accepting a false null hypothesis is known as:
e: Type II error is the failure to detect a real effect.

q: The commonly used level of significance in social research is:
e: The five per cent level is the conventional criterion.

q: In a positively skewed distribution the relation among averages is:
o: Mode is greater than median which is greater than mean
Mean is greater than median which is greater than mode
e: A long right tail pulls the mean above the median and mode.

q: The measure describing the peakedness of a distribution is:
e: Kurtosis compares the peak and tails with the normal curve.

q: Which of the following is NOT a measure of dispersion?
e: The median is a measure of central tendency, not of dispersion.

q: A pie diagram is most suitable for showing:
e: Pie charts display parts of a total as sectors of a circle.

q: The graph obtained by joining the midpoints of the tops of histogram bars is a:
e: A frequency polygon is a line graph of a frequency distribution.

q: The cumulative frequency curve is known as the:
e: The median can be read from the point where the two ogives intersect.

q: The graphical device used to display the relationship between two variables is a:
e: A scatter diagram plots paired values of two variables.

q: Informed consent in research means that the respondent:
o: Agrees to take part after understanding the purpose and risks
e: Voluntary and informed agreement is a basic ethical requirement.

q: Presenting another author's work as one's own is called:
e: Plagiarism is a serious breach of research ethics.

q: Anonymity in research means that:
o: The identity of the respondent is not known even to the researcher
e: Confidentiality, in contrast, means identity is known but not disclosed.

q: In a research report, the detailed questionnaire is usually placed in the:
e: Supporting material such as tools and tables goes into appendices.

q: The brief summary of the whole study placed at the beginning of a report is the:
e: An abstract states the problem, method, findings and conclusion in brief.

q: The alphabetical list of works cited at the end of a research report is the:
e: The bibliography or reference list documents all sources used.

q: Which of the following is the correct sequence of steps in social research?
o: Problem, hypothesis, research design, data collection, analysis, report
Hypothesis, problem, data collection, analysis, report
e: The problem is defined first and the report comes last.

q: Reasoning that moves from a general theory to a specific testable hypothesis is:
e: Deduction goes from the general to the particular.

q: Reasoning that moves from specific observations to a general conclusion is:
e: Induction builds generalisations from repeated observations.

q: Grounded theory, in which theory emerges from data, was developed by:
e: Barney Glaser and Anselm Strauss set out the method in 1967.

q: The use of more than one method or data source to study the same problem is:
e: Triangulation strengthens the credibility of findings.

q: A researcher wishes to study the effect of a nutrition programme by comparing children who receive it with a matched group who do not. This design is:
o: Experimental design with a control group
e: A control group isolates the effect of the intervention.

q: A CDPO wants to track the growth of the same hundred children from birth to five years. The suitable design is:
e: Repeated measurement of the same children over time is a panel design.

q: A researcher studying commercial sex workers obtains new respondents through referrals from earlier ones. This is:
e: Snowball sampling is used where a sampling frame is unavailable.

q: A student wants a sample that mirrors the religious composition of a district and randomly selects within each religious group. This is:
e: Strata are formed first and random selection is made within each.

q: An investigator studies one severely malnourished child in depth, tracing family history, diet and environment. The method used is:
e: The case study gives a holistic account of a single unit.

q: A team asks village women to identify their own problems, collect data and plan solutions with them. This is:
e: The community participates in enquiry and in the resulting action.

q: A researcher measures religion as Hindu, Muslim, Christian and Other. The scale used is:
e: The categories classify without implying any order.

q: A study records household monthly income in rupees. The level of measurement is:
e: Income has equal intervals and a meaningful absolute zero.

q: A researcher finds that scores on her scale differ widely when the same respondents are retested a week later. The tool lacks:
e: Inconsistency across administrations indicates poor reliability.

q: An investigator observes an Anganwadi from outside without taking part in its activities. This is:
e: The observer remains detached from the group being observed.

q: A researcher reports individual respondents' names along with their answers in a published study. This violates:
e: Identifying respondents without consent breaches research ethics.

q: Exploratory research refers to:
o: Study undertaken to gain familiarity with a little known problem
Observation while sharing in the life of the group studied
Study that portrays the characteristics of a group or situation
Method in which theory is generated from systematically analysed data
e: It is also called formulative research.

q: M. N. Srinivas is known for writing:
e: An ethnographic account based on long fieldwork.

q: Which of the following is true of Standard deviation?
o: Testing the research tools before the main enquiry
Measuring the average spread of values around the mean
Showing the shape of a frequency distribution as a line
Summarising a distribution by its balancing point
e: It is expressed in the same units as the data.

q: 'Systematic and objective study of social phenomena' best describes which concept?
e: It applies scientific procedures to social questions.

q: 'The Design of Experiments' — identify the author.
e: It introduced randomisation and analysis of variance.

q: 'The Focused Interview' was written by:
e: It described the technique behind modern focus groups.

q: What is meant by 'Exploratory research'?
o: Study undertaken to gain familiarity with a little known problem
Degree to which a tool measures the theoretical concept intended
Difference between a sample value and the true population value
Observation while sharing in the life of the group studied
e: It is also called formulative research.

q: Extraneous variable refers to:
o: Measurement of interpersonal choices within a group
Variable deliberately held constant during a study
Outside variable capable of influencing the result
Provisional assumption adopted to guide initial enquiry
e: If uncontrolled it threatens internal validity.

q: Adolphe Quetelet contributed to the discipline mainly through:
o: Development of sociometry and the sociogram
Criteria of trustworthiness for qualitative enquiry
Mathematical formulation of the normal distribution
Application of statistics to social phenomena
e: He advanced the idea of the average man.

q: Sociogram mainly helps in:
o: Displaying patterns of choice and rejection within a group
Providing a baseline for comparison in an experiment
Predicting the value of one variable from another
Showing the shape of a frequency distribution as a line
e: It is the visual output of sociometry.

q: What is meant by 'Descriptive research'?
o: Study that portrays the characteristics of a group or situation
Difference between a sample value and the true population value
Study of a population at a single point in time
Observation while sharing in the life of the group studied
e: It answers what, who, where and when.

q: Which item corresponds to 'Editing'?
o: Type of question offering fixed response alternatives
Survey providing India's fertility and health indicators
Section of a report containing the questionnaire
Process of examining collected schedules for completeness
e: It precedes coding and tabulation.

q: Quantitative research refers to:
o: Measurement with equal intervals but an arbitrary zero
Enquiry based on numerical measurement and statistical analysis
Enquiry directed at solving an immediate practical problem
Enquiry based on meanings, words and detailed description
e: It emphasises objectivity, sampling and generalisation.

q: Choose the correct option regarding Statistic used with two independent group means.
e: It assumes approximately normal distributions.

q: First step in the research process is:
o: Selection and formulation of the research problem
Possible mismatch with the present research problem
Highest value minus the lowest value
e: Everything else follows from a clearly defined problem.

q: What is meant by 'Directional hypothesis'?
o: Variable deliberately held constant during a study
Hypothesis predicting the direction of a difference
Information collected first hand by the investigator
Variable measured as the effect or outcome
e: It is tested with a one-tailed test.
